sentences.zh: 鄭岳，字汝華，莆田人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yue, styled Ruhua, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yue, whose style was Ruhua, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，改刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, then transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 董天錫偕錦衣千戶張福決囚，福坐天錫上，嶽言其非體。

translations.literal: Dong Tianxi, together with the brocade-clad guard commander Zhang Fu, adjudicated prisoners; Fu was seated above Tianxi, and Yue said this was improper.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Tianxi and the brocade-clad guard commander Zhang Fu jointly tried prisoners, Fu was placed above Tianxi; Yue protested that this violated proper order.

sentences.zh: 且言：「糾劾非鎮監職，而董讓行之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Impeachment is not the duty of frontier commissioners, yet Dong had them carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Impeachment is not within a frontier commissioner's remit, yet Dong had them do it anyway.

sentences.zh: 太常本禮部屬，而崔誌端專之。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices properly belongs under the Ministry of Rites, yet Cui Zhiduan monopolized it.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices properly falls under the Ministry of Rites, yet Cui Zhiduan kept it under his own control.

sentences.zh: 內外效尤，益無忌憚」。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court they took this as a model, growing ever more brazen."
translations.idiomatic: Officials within and beyond the capital followed suit, and grew ever more reckless."

sentences.zh: 忤旨，系獄。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His words angered the throne and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 尚書周經、侍郎許進等救，不聽。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jing, Vice Minister Xu Jin, and others interceded, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jing, Vice Minister Xu Jin, and others pleaded for him, but the emperor refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 贖杖還職。

translations.literal: He ransomed himself with a beating and returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He paid a fine to commute the rod punishment and resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 尋進員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 許進督師大同，貴近惡其剛方，議代之。

translations.literal: Xu Jin commanded the army at Datong; powerful men near the throne hated his stern integrity and plotted to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: While Xu Jin directed operations at Datong, court favorites resented his upright rigor and schemed to remove him.

sentences.zh: 罷職總兵官趙袴謀起用，京軍屢出無功。

translations.literal: The dismissed regional commander Zhao Kua sought reinstatement, and the capital army had been sent out repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: The disgraced regional commander Zhao Kua maneuvered for a comeback, while repeated sorties by the capital army had achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 嶽言進不可代，袴不可用，京軍不可出。

translations.literal: Yue said Jin must not be replaced, Kua must not be employed, and the capital army must not be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Yue argued that Jin should not be replaced, Kua should not be reappointed, and the capital army should not be deployed again.

sentences.zh: 朝論韙之。

translations.literal: Court opinion approved his views.
translations.idiomatic: The court endorsed his position.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣僉事，歸宗藩侵地於民。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner in Huguang and restored to the people land seized by princely estates.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner in Huguang, he returned to commoners lands that princely estates had seized.

sentences.zh: 施州夷民相仇殺者，有司以叛告。

translations.literal: When Yi tribesmen in Shizhou killed one another in vendetta, local officials reported rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizhou, tribal people who had killed one another in blood feuds were reported by local officials as rebels.

sentences.zh: 嶽擒治其魁，余悉縱遣。

translations.literal: Yue seized and punished the ringleaders and released all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrested and punished the leaders and set the rest free.

sentences.zh: 荊、嶽饑，勸富民出粟，馳河泊禁。

translations.literal: When Jing and Yue [prefectures] suffered famine, he urged wealthy households to release grain and urgently lifted restrictions on river transport.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in the Jing and Yue regions, he urged the wealthy to sell grain and quickly eased the ban on river transport.

sentences.zh: 屬縣輸糧遠衛，率二石致一石。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties shipping grain to distant guards commonly delivered only one shi for every two sent.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate counties shipped grain to distant guards, they often delivered only one shi for every two dispatched.

sentences.zh: 嶽以其直給衛，而留粟備振，民乃獲濟。

translations.literal: Yue paid the guards the cash value and kept the grain for relief, and the people were thereby saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yue paid the guards in cash and retained the grain for relief stores, so the people were finally able to survive.

sentences.zh: 正德初，擢廣西副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was promoted to vice commissioner in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was raised to vice commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 土官岑猛當徙福建，據田州不肯徙。

translations.literal: The native official Cen Meng was to be relocated to Fujian but held Tianzhou and refused to move.
translations.idiomatic: The native official Cen Meng was ordered to Fujian but occupied Tianzhou and would not relocate.

sentences.zh: 岳許為奏改近地，猛乃請自效。

translations.literal: Yue promised to memorialize for a transfer to a nearer place, and Meng then offered to serve on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Yue promised to seek a nearer posting for him in memorial, whereupon Meng volunteered his service.

sentences.zh: 尋改廣東。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 遷江西按察使，就遷左布政使。

translations.literal: He was moved to Jiangxi as surveillance commissioner and then directly promoted to left administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became surveillance commissioner in Jiangxi and was soon promoted to left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宸濠奪民田億萬計，民立砦自保。

translations.literal: Prince Ning seized countless fields from the people, and the people built stockades to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning had seized untold tracts of commoners' land, and the people fortified stockades in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 宸濠欲兵之，嶽持不可。

translations.literal: When Prince Ning wished to send troops against them, Yue held that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning wanted to attack them by force, Yue insisted that he must not.

sentences.zh: 會提學副使李夢陽與巡按御史江萬實相訐，嶽承檄按之。

translations.literal: As the education intendant Li Mengyang and the touring censor Jiang Wanshi were mutually accusing one another, Yue received orders to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When education intendant Li Mengyang and touring censor Jiang Wanshi traded accusations, Yue was ordered to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 夢陽執嶽親信吏，言嶽子澐受賕，欲因以脅嶽。

translations.literal: Mengyang seized Yue's trusted clerk and said Yue's son Yun had taken bribes, intending thereby to coerce Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang arrested Yue's trusted clerk and claimed Yue's son Yun had accepted bribes, hoping to intimidate Yue.

sentences.zh: 宸濠因助夢陽奏其事，囚掠澐。

translations.literal: Prince Ning therefore aided Mengyang in memorializing the matter and had Yun seized and tortured.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning backed Mengyang's memorial and had Yun seized and tortured.

sentences.zh: 巡撫任漢顧慮不能決，帝遣大理卿燕忠會給事中黎奭按問。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Ren Han hesitated and could not decide; the emperor sent Court of Judicial Review director Yan Zhong, together with supervising secretary Li Yi, to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Ren Han wavered; the emperor dispatched Court of Judicial Review director Yan Zhong and supervising secretary Li Yi to conduct a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 忠等奏勘嶽子私有跡，而夢陽挾制撫、按，俱宜斥。

translations.literal: Zhong and the others reported that investigation showed traces of private gain by Yue's son, while Mengyang had coerced the grand coordinator and censor—both sides should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: They found that Yue's son had indeed profited privately, while Mengyang had bullied the grand coordinator and censor; both parties, they ruled, should be removed.

sentences.zh: 嶽遂奪官為民。

translations.literal: Yue was therefore stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was stripped of office and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 宸濠敗，中外交薦，起四川布政使。

translations.literal: After Prince Ning's defeat, court and frontier alike recommended him, and he was appointed administration commissioner in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Ning's rebellion collapsed, officials at court and on the frontier recommended him, and he was appointed administration commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 以憂不赴。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post because of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up the appointment owing to bereavement.

sentences.zh: 劉玉，字鹹栗，萬安人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, styled Xianli, was a native of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, whose style was Xianli, came from Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖廣衡，永樂末進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guangheng passed the jinshi at the end of the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guangheng took the jinshi in the closing years of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 正統間，以刑部郎中出修浙江荒政，積粟數百萬，督治陂塘為旱澇備。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period, as a director in the Ministry of Justice he went out to manage famine relief in Zhejiang, amassing millions of piculs of grain and supervising dikes and ponds as provision against drought and flood.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong, as a director in the Ministry of Justice he went to Zhejiang to manage famine relief, stockpiled millions of piculs of grain, and oversaw dikes and ponds against drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，歷左副都御史，鎮守陜西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign he successively served as left vice censor-in-chief, defending Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingtai he rose to left vice censor-in-chief and defended Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 請遇災傷，毋俟勘報，即除其賦，庶有司不得借覆核陰行科率，從之。

translations.literal: He requested that when disaster or injury struck, taxes not wait for investigation and report but be remitted at once, so that officials could not use re-verification as a pretext for hidden exactions; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that when disaster struck, levies be remitted without waiting for investigation, lest officials use re-verification as cover for hidden exactions; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 還治院事。

translations.literal: He returned to handle affairs at the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to direct affairs at the censorate.

sentences.zh: 福建、浙江盜起，命往督兵捕。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Fujian and Zhejiang, he was ordered to supervise troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Fujian and Zhejiang, he was sent to command pursuit operations.

sentences.zh: 議創壽寧縣於官臺山，以清盜窟。

translations.literal: He proposed creating Shouning County on Guantai Mountain to clear out the bandits' lair.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing Shouning County on Guantai Mountain to eliminate the bandits' refuge.

sentences.zh: 討平處州賊。

translations.literal: He campaigned and pacified the bandits of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed and pacified the bandits of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 已，復巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: Later he again served as grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He later served again as grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 居官以廉節稱。

translations.literal: In office he was known for integrity and self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career he was famed for integrity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 終刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He ended his career as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 父喬，成化初進士。

translations.literal: His father Qiao passed the jinshi at the beginning of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao received the jinshi early in the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 累官湖廣左布政使。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to left administration commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left administration commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 玉登弘治九年進士，授輝縣知縣。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi and was appointed magistrate of Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took the jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi and was appointed magistrate of Huixian.

sentences.zh: 發粟振饑，奏蠲虛稅，復業者千家。

translations.literal: He released grain to relieve famine, memorialized to remit empty levies, and a thousand households resumed their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He opened granaries in famine, secured remission of hollow levies, and a thousand households returned to their trades.

sentences.zh: 擢御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to censor.

sentences.zh: 初，孫伯堅、金琦、王寧皆以傳奉得官，已，又以指揮胡震為都指揮，分守通州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Bojian, Jin Qi, and Wang Ning had all received office through personal appointment from the throne; afterward the commandant Hu Zhen was also made regional commander to guard Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Bojian, Jin Qi, and Wang Ning had all gained posts through direct imperial favor; later the commandant Hu Zhen was likewise made regional commander at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉抗疏言：「傳奉不已，繼之內批，累聖德，乞皆罷之。」

translations.literal: Yu submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Personal appointments continue without end, followed by inner-court rescripts; this steadily erodes imperial virtue—let all such practices be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: In a bold memorial he wrote: "Favored appointments never cease, and inner rescripts follow; this steadily wears away the emperor's virtue—I beg that all of it be stopped.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召為左僉都御史。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, Yu was summoned as left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, Yu was summoned as left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 論遏亂功，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: For merit in checking disorder he was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For service in quelling disorder he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年改左。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was moved to the left post.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as left and right vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 初，偕九卿爭興獻帝不宜稱皇，及帝欲考獻帝，又偕廷臣伏闕哭爭。

translations.literal: Earlier, together with the nine ministers he had disputed that the Prince of Xing should not be styled emperor; when the emperor wished to honor the Prince of Xing as his father, he again joined the court in kneeling at the palace gate to weep and protest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had joined the nine ministers in denying the Prince of Xing the title of emperor; when the emperor sought to honor his birth father, Yu again joined court officials weeping and protesting at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 六年秋坐李福達獄削籍，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he was struck from the rolls in the Li Fuda case and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year he was removed from the register in the Li Fuda affair and died at home.

sentences.zh: 玉所居僅庇風雨。

translations.literal: Where Yu lived afforded barely shelter from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling scarcely kept out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 天文、地理、兵制、刑律皆有論著。

translations.literal: He wrote treatises on astronomy, geography, military institutions, and penal law.
translations.idiomatic: He left writings on astronomy, geography, military institutions, and penal law.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈刑部尚書，謚端毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made minister of justice and given the posthumous title Duanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he was posthumously made minister of justice with the posthumous title Duanyi.

sentences.zh: 子愨，南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Zi Que served as right vice minister of works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi Que served as right vice minister of works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 歷官亦有聲。

translations.literal: In office he too enjoyed a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He too won repute in office.

sentences.zh: 汪元錫，字天啟，婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanxi, styled Tianqi, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanxi, whose style was Tianqi, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received the jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 三遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 陜西鎮守中官廖鸞族子鎧，冒功為錦衣千戶，隨鸞於陜。

translations.literal: In Shaanxi, Luan, a kinsman of the eunuch frontier commissioner Liao Luan, falsely claimed merit and was made a commander in the brocade-clad guard, following Luan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi, Kai—a kinsman of frontier eunuch Liao Luan—had falsely claimed merit and been made a commander in the brocade-clad guard, accompanying Luan in the province.

sentences.zh: 元錫爭之，言鎧父鵬已亂中州，勿使鎧復亂陜右。

translations.literal: Yuanxi protested, saying Kai's father Peng had already thrown the central plains into disorder and that Kai must not be allowed to disorder Shaanxi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi objected, saying Kai's father Peng had already ravaged the central provinces and Kai must not be allowed to do the same in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 乞征還鸞，置鎧父子於理。

translations.literal: He begged that Luan be recalled and that father and son be brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Luan be recalled and father and son punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 偏頭關之捷，錄功太濫，偕同官言太監張忠、總兵官劉暉等不宜賞。

translations.literal: For the victory at Piantou Pass the recording of merit was too lavish; together with colleagues he said the eunuch Zhang Zhong and regional commander Liu Hui and others should not be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Piantou Pass, merit was recorded too generously; with fellow officials he argued that eunuch Zhang Zhong and regional commander Liu Hui should not receive rewards.

sentences.zh: 湖廣鎮守太監杜甫請巡歷所部，帝許之，元錫等據祖制力爭。

translations.literal: The Huguang frontier eunuch Du Fu requested to tour his jurisdiction, and the emperor assented; Yuanxi and others cited ancestral regulations and protested vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huguang frontier eunuch Du Fu asked to tour his command, the emperor agreed; Yuanxi and others cited ancestral precedent and protested forcefully.

sentences.zh: 帝幸昌平、宣府、大同，元錫偕同官邢寰累疏諫；

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Changping, Xuanfu, and Datong, Yuanxi together with colleague Xing Huan submitted repeated remonstrances;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured Changping, Xuanfu, and Datong, Yuanxi and his colleague Xing Huan sent repeated remonstrances;

sentences.zh: 復言宣府守將朱振等皆扈從西巡，寇乘虛入塞，何以禦之？

translations.literal: he also said that the Xuanfu garrison commanders Zhu Zhen and others were all accompanying the western tour, so if raiders entered the passes empty, how could they be resisted?
translations.idiomatic: he also warned that garrison commanders such as Zhu Zhen of Xuanfu were all away on the western tour—if raiders entered the passes, who would hold them?

sentences.zh: 已，聞帝將選禁軍親征四海治部寇，復極陳不可。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that the emperor would select the palace guard for a personal campaign against the Sihai Zhibu bandits, he again memorialized forcefully that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the emperor meant to lead the palace guard personally against the Sihai Zhibu rebels, he again protested in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 安遠侯柳文鎮湖廣，奏攜參隨七十余人，元錫乞寢所奏。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Wen, commanding Huguang, memorialized that he wished to bring more than seventy attendants; Yuanxi begged that the memorial be shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Anyuan Liu Wen, stationed in Huguang, asked to bring over seventy retainers, Yuanxi urged that the request be denied.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，以應州之捷大賚文武群臣。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, the victory at Yingzhou was made the occasion for lavish rewards to civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return to Beijing, the Yingzhou victory was celebrated with lavish gifts to the entire court.

sentences.zh: 元錫等言：「是役殺邊民無算，六軍多傷。

translations.literal: Yuanxi and others said: "In that campaign countless frontier people were killed and the six armies suffered many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi and others wrote: "That campaign killed untold numbers on the frontier and left the six armies badly mauled.

sentences.zh: 今君臣欣喜交賀，而軍民系賊庭，南向號哭，臣等何忍受賜？」

translations.literal: Now ruler and ministers rejoice and congratulate one another, while soldiers and civilians are held in the enemy camp, weeping and crying to the south—how can we bear to accept rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet court and throne now exchange congratulations while troops and people languish in enemy hands, wailing toward the south—how can we accept reward?

sentences.zh: 中旨以納粟都指揮馬昊守備儀真，復遣內官分守潼關、山海關，駕又幸大喜峰口，欲招三衛花當、把兒孫，元錫等皆抗章諫。

translations.literal: By secret edict Ma Hao, who had paid grain for appointment as regional commander, was made garrison commander at Yizhen; eunuchs were again sent to garrison Tong Pass and Shanhai Pass separately; the carriage again visited Daxingfeng Pass, intending to summon the Three Guards Huadang and Ba'ersun—Yuanxi and others all submitted remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict made grain-purchased commander Ma Hao garrison Yizhen; eunuchs were again posted to Tong and Shanhai passes; the emperor again visited Daxingfeng Pass to summon Huadang and Ba'ersun of the Three Guards—and Yuanxi and others remonstrated on every count.

sentences.zh: 帝欲南幸，舒芬、黃鞏切諫得罪，給事御史遂不敢爭。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to tour the south, Shu Fen and Huang Gong remonstrated sharply and were punished; supervising secretaries and censors then dared not dispute.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a southern tour, Shu Fen and Huang Gong protested bluntly and were punished, after which the supervising secretaries and censors fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及帝將親征宸濠，元錫復諫沮。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to campaign personally against Prince Ning, Yuanxi again remonstrated to dissuade him.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to lead the campaign against Prince Ning in person, Yuanxi again tried to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 宸濠就執，元錫、寰偕六科馳疏請回鑾。

translations.literal: After Prince Ning was captured, Yuanxi and Huan together with the six bureaus sent urgent memorials asking that the imperial carriage return.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince Ning was taken, Yuanxi and Huan with the six bureaus rushed memorials begging the emperor to turn homeward.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝在南京，元錫等復屢申前請，且言：「供億繁費，使牒旁午。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, while the emperor was at Nanjing, Yuanxi and others repeatedly pressed their earlier requests and said: "Supplies are costly and wasteful, and orders fly back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, with the emperor still at Nanjing, Yuanxi and others renewed their pleas, warning that costs were ruinous and orders unending.

sentences.zh: 奸宄冒官校，少女充離宮。

translations.literal: Evildoers pose as official envoys, and young women fill the detached palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians masquerade as imperial agents, and young women stock the pleasure palaces.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以宗社為重，專事逸遊，豈能長保天下。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not hold the altars of state paramount but devotes yourself to idle travel—how can you long preserve the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty values pleasure travel above the altars of state, how will the empire endure?

sentences.zh: 語甚危切。

translations.literal: Their language was very stern.
translations.idiomatic: Their words were stark and urgent.

sentences.zh: 中旨以內官晁進、楊保分守蘭州、肅州，元錫等言：「二州逼強寇，不可增官守，累居民。」

translations.literal: By secret edict the eunuchs Chao Jin and Yang Bao were sent to garrison Lanzhou and Suzhou separately; Yuanxi and others said: "The two prefectures press upon powerful enemies—adding garrison officials only burdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: Secret orders posted eunuchs Chao Jin and Yang Bao at Lanzhou and Suzhou; Yuanxi protested that both regions bordered powerful enemies and extra officials would only oppress the people.

sentences.zh: 群小不悅，矯旨責之。

translations.literal: The petty men were displeased and forged an edict rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Court favorites were angered and had a forged edict castigate them.

sentences.zh: 詔改團營西官廳為威武團練營，以江彬、許泰等提督之，別擇地為團營教場。

translations.literal: An edict changed the western office of the Tuan barracks into the Weiwu training camp, with Jiang Bin and Xu Tai and others placed in overall command, and another site chosen as the Tuan training ground.
translations.idiomatic: An edict turned the Tuan barracks' western office into the Weiwu training camp under Jiang Bin, Xu Tai, and others, and set aside new ground for drill.

sentences.zh: 元錫言：「拓地則擾居民，興工則費財力，以朝廷自將之軍而彬等概加提督，則僭名分。」

translations.literal: Yuanxi said: "Expanding the site will disturb residents; launching works will waste wealth and labor; to place Bin and others in overall command of troops the court itself commands is to usurp rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi argued that expanding the grounds would harass the people, construction would drain the treasury, and putting Bin and others over troops the throne itself commanded was rank usurpation.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，事已。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，疏言：「都督郤永以附江彬下獄，宜釋而用之。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, Yuanxi memorialized: "Regional commander Xi Yong is imprisoned for following Jiang Bin and should be released and employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiajing accession he memorialized that Regional Commander Xi Yong, imprisoned for siding with Jiang Bin, should be released and used.

sentences.zh: 錦衣都指揮郭鰲等十人皆彬黨，宜下獄治。」

translations.literal: Ten men including brocade-clad guard commander Guo Ao were all Bin's partisans and should be imprisoned and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Ten men including brocade-clad commander Guo Ao, all Bin's followers, should be jailed and tried.

sentences.zh: 鹹報可。

translations.literal: The response approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved in full.

sentences.zh: 張銑、許泰系獄，帝忽宥其死。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian and Xu Tai were imprisoned, but the emperor suddenly pardoned them from death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian and Xu Tai were in prison when the emperor suddenly spared their lives.

sentences.zh: 元錫爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Yuanxi protested, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi objected, but the emperor would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 屢遷至太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，帝以李福達獄下三法司於理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing the emperor sent the three judicial offices to try the Li Fuda case.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing the emperor referred the Li Fuda case to the three judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 元錫不能平，有後言，聞於張璁，並下獄奪職。

translations.literal: Yuanxi could not accept the verdict and spoke afterward; word reached Zhang Cong, and he was imprisoned and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi could not accept the outcome and spoke afterward; Zhang Cong heard of it and had him imprisoned and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後用薦起故官。

translations.literal: Later, on recommendation, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to office on recommendation.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部左、右侍郎，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as left and right vice minister of revenue, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right vice minister of revenue, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 邢寰，黃梅人。

translations.literal: Xing Huan was a native of Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Huan came from Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 數言事，有直聲。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke on affairs of state and enjoyed a reputation for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke often on public affairs and won a name for outspoken integrity.

sentences.zh: 寇天敘，字子惇，楡次人。

translations.literal: Kou Tianxu, styled Zidun, was a native of Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Tianxu, whose style was Zidun, came from Yuci.

sentences.zh: 由鄕舉入太學。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy via the provincial route.

sentences.zh: 與崔銑、呂柟善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Cui Qian and Lü Zha.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Cui Qian and Lü Zha.

sentences.zh: 登正德三年進士，除南京大理評事，進寺副。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde, was appointed reviewer at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to vice director of the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi, became a reviewer at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 累遷應天府丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice magistrate of Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to vice magistrate of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 武宗駐南京，從官衛士十余萬，日費金萬計，近幸求索倍之。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor stayed at Nanjing, attendants and guards numbered more than a hundred thousand, costing ten thousand taels of silver a day, and the emperor's favorites demanded twice as much.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor lodged at Nanjing, his entourage and guards exceeded a hundred thousand and cost ten thousand taels a day, while favorites demanded double.

sentences.zh: 尹齊宗道憂懼卒，天敘攝其事，日青衣皂帽坐堂上。

translations.literal: Magistrate Qi Zongdao died of anxiety; Tianxu took charge of affairs, daily wearing blue robes and black caps to sit in court.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Qi Zongdao died of worry; Tianxu took over, sitting in court each day in plain blue dress and black cap.

sentences.zh: 江彬使者至，好語之曰：「民窮官帑乏，無可結歡，丞專待譴耳。」

translations.literal: When Jiang Bin's envoys arrived, Tianxu spoke to them kindly: "The people are destitute and the treasury empty—there is nothing with which to win favor; the vice magistrate awaits only punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Bin's messengers came, he told them gently: "The people are poor and the treasury bare—there is nothing to offer; this vice magistrate awaits only reprimand.

sentences.zh: 彬使累至皆然，彬亦止。

translations.literal: Bin's envoys came repeatedly and always received the same answer, and Bin too desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's envoys came again and again and always got the same reply, until Bin himself gave up.

sentences.zh: 他權幸有求，則曰：「俟若奏即予。」

translations.literal: When other powerful favorites made demands, he would say: "Wait until you memorialize and it will be granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: When other favorites demanded favors, he said: "Wait until you memorialize and you shall have it.

sentences.zh: 禁軍攫民物，天敘與兵部尚書喬宇選拳勇者與搏戲。

translations.literal: When palace troops seized civilians' goods, Tianxu and Minister of War Qiao Yu chose strong men to wrestle with them.
translations.idiomatic: When palace soldiers seized people's goods, Tianxu and War Minister Qiao Yu picked sturdy men to wrestle them.

sentences.zh: 禁軍卒受傷，慚且畏，不敢橫。

translations.literal: The palace soldiers were wounded, ashamed and afraid, and no longer acted arrogantly.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were hurt, ashamed and afraid, and dared not bully the people again.

sentences.zh: 其隨事禁制多類此。

translations.literal: His prohibitions on such matters were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his restraints on abuse followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 駕駐九月，南京不大困者，天敘與宇力也。

translations.literal: During the nine months the emperor stayed there, Nanjing was not greatly distressed—this was due to Tianxu and Yu's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: For the nine months of the imperial stay, Nanjing did not collapse—thanks to Tianxu and Yu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，以右僉都御史巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing he became right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 未行，改鄖陽。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he was transferred to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he was reassigned to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 甫二月，又改甘肅。

translations.literal: After only two months he was again transferred to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was moved again to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 回賊犯山丹，督將士擒其長脫脫木兒。

translations.literal: When Hui rebels attacked Shandan, he directed officers and soldiers to capture their leader Tuotuomu'er.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebels struck Shandan, he led troops to seize their chief Tuotuomu'er.

sentences.zh: 西域貢獅子、犀牛、西狗，天敘請卻之，不聽。

translations.literal: The Western Regions presented lions, rhinoceroses, and western dogs; Tianxu asked that these be refused, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Regions sent lions, rhinoceroses, and exotic dogs, Tianxu asked to refuse them, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 寇入固原，撃敗之，斬首百餘。

translations.literal: When raiders entered Guyuan, he defeated them and beheaded more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits entered Guyuan, he routed them and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 又討平大盜王居等，累賜銀幣。

translations.literal: He also campaigned and pacified the great bandit Wang Ju and others, and was repeatedly rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He also suppressed the great outlaw Wang Ju and others and received repeated gifts of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 織造太監至，有司議奏罷之。

translations.literal: When the imperial weaving eunuch arrived, local officials proposed memorializing to abolish the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial weaving eunuch arrived, local officials wanted to memorialize for his recall.

sentences.zh: 天敘曰：「甫至遽請罷，即不罷，焰且益張。」

translations.literal: Tianxu said: "He has only just arrived and you immediately ask to remove him—even if he is not removed, his arrogance will only grow.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxu said: "He has barely arrived and you already ask to dismiss him—if he stays, his swagger will only swell.

sentences.zh: 會歲祲，乃請蠲租稅，發粟振饑民；

translations.literal: As famine struck that year, he then asked to remit rent and taxes and release grain to relieve the starving;
translations.idiomatic: When famine came that year, he sought remission of taxes and grain relief;

sentences.zh: 因言織造非儉歲所宜設，帝立召還。

translations.literal: he also said that imperial weaving was unsuitable in a frugal year, and the emperor immediately recalled the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: he added that imperial weaving was wrong in a lean year, and the emperor at once recalled the eunuch.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部右侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: He served as right vice minister of war and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice minister of war and died in office.

sentences.zh: 家貧，喪事不具。

translations.literal: His family was poor and funeral arrangements were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: His household was so poor the funeral could not be properly arranged.

sentences.zh: 天敘在太學時，嘗聞父疾，馳六晝夜抵家，父疾亦廖。

translations.literal: While Tianxu was in the academy, he once heard his father was ill, galloped home in six days and nights, and his father's illness also abated.
translations.idiomatic: At the academy he once heard his father was ill, rode home in six days and nights, and found his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 唐胄，字平侯，瓊山人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhou, styled Pinghou, was a native of Qiongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhou, whose style was Pinghou, came from Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾斥諸服除久不赴官者，坐奪職。

translations.literal: Liu Jin dismissed all who had completed mourning but long failed to resume office; Zhou was stripped of office on this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin purged officials who had finished mourning but delayed return; Zhou lost his post thereby.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，召用，以母老不出。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, Zhou was summoned but did not take office because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was recalled but stayed away while his mother lived.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏諫內官織造，請為宋死節臣趙與珞追謚立祠。

translations.literal: He memorialized against eunuch weaving and asked that posthumous honors and a shrine be granted to Zhao Yuluo, who had died loyal in the Song.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against eunuch weaving and sought posthumous honors and a shrine for the Song martyr Zhao Yuluo.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎，遷廣西提學僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director and moved to education intendant in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director and made education intendant in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 令土官及瑤、蠻悉遣子入學。

translations.literal: He ordered native officials and Yao and Man tribes all to send sons to school.
translations.idiomatic: He required native chiefs and Yao and Man peoples to send sons to the schools.

sentences.zh: 擢金騰副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner at Jinteng.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to vice commissioner at Jinteng.

sentences.zh: 土酋莽信虐，計擒之。

translations.literal: The native chief Mang Xin was cruel; Zhou plotted and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted the capture of the brutal native chief Mang Xin.

sentences.zh: 木邦、孟養構兵，胄遣使宣諭，木邦遂獻地。

translations.literal: When Mubang and Mengyang went to war, Zhou sent envoys to instruct them, and Mubang then ceded territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Mubang and Mengyang fought, Zhou sent envoys; Mubang then yielded land.

sentences.zh: 屢遷廣西左布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left administration commissioner in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left administration commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 官軍討古田賊，久無功，胄遣使撫之其魁曰：「是前唐使君令吾子入學者。」

translations.literal: Government troops campaigned against Gutian bandits for a long time without success; Zhou sent envoys to pacify them, and their leader said: "This is the former Tang envoy who had our sons enter school.
translations.idiomatic: Troops had long failed against Gutian bandits; Zhou sent envoys, and their chief said: "This is the Tang envoy who sent our sons to school.

sentences.zh: 即解甲。

translations.literal: They at once laid down arms.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately disarmed.

sentences.zh: 擢右副都御史，巡撫南、贛，移山東。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Nan and Gan, and transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Nan and Gan, then moved to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 遷南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to right vice minister of revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice minister of revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十五年改北部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to the northern ministry and promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he moved to the northern ministry as left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 帝以安南久不貢，將致討，郭勛復贊之。

translations.literal: Because Annam had long failed to offer tribute, the emperor intended to chastise it, and Guo Xun again urged this.
translations.idiomatic: As Annam had long withheld tribute, the emperor planned punishment, and Guo Xun again urged war.

sentences.zh: 詔遣錦衣官問狀，中外嚴兵待發。

translations.literal: An edict sent brocade-clad officials to investigate; inside and outside the court strict preparations for war were made.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts sent brocade-clad agents to inquire; court and country braced for war.

sentences.zh: 胄上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhou submitted a remonstrance saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhou memorialized in protest:

sentences.zh: 今日之事，若欲其修貢而已，兵不必用，官亦無容遣。

translations.literal: "If today's affair aims only to secure tribute, troops need not be used and officials need not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: "If we only want tribute restored, we need neither armies nor envoys.

sentences.zh: 若欲討之，則有不可者七，請一一陳之：

translations.literal: If we wish to chastise them, there are seven reasons why we should not—let me set them forth one by one:
translations.idiomatic: If we mean to attack, seven reasons forbid it—hear them in order:

sentences.zh: 古帝王不以中國之治治蠻夷，故安南不征，著在《祖訓》。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors did not govern barbarians with the same methods used to govern China; therefore Annam was not to be attacked—this is recorded in the Ancestral Injunctions.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage-kings did not rule barbarians as they ruled China; Annam was not to be attacked—so the Ancestral Injunctions declare.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: First.
translations.idiomatic: First.

sentences.zh: 太宗既滅黎季筼，求陳氏後不得，始郡縣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, having destroyed Li Jicang, could not find a descendant of the Chen house and therefore made the region commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong destroyed Li Jicang, found no Chen heir, and made the land into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 後兵連不解，仁廟每以為恨。

translations.literal: Warfare continued without end afterward, and Emperor Renzong always regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: War dragged on endlessly, and Renzong always regretted it.

sentences.zh: 章皇帝成先誌，棄而不守，今日當率循。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang fulfilled the earlier will and abandoned the territory; today we should follow that precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang fulfilled that intent and let the land go; we should follow his example.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: Second.
translations.idiomatic: Second.

sentences.zh: 外夷分爭，中國之福。

translations.literal: When outer barbarians fight among themselves, it is China's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When outer peoples fight each other, China profits.

sentences.zh: 安南自五代至元，更曲、劉、紹、吳、丁、黎、李、陳八姓，叠興叠廢，而嶺南外警遂稀。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties through the Yuan, Annam saw eight surnames—Qu, Liu, Shao, Wu, Ding, Li, and Chen—rise and fall in turn, and frontier alarms in Lingnan grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties to the Yuan, eight houses—Qu, Liu, Shao, Wu, Ding, Li, and Chen—rose and fell in Annam, and alarms on the Lingnan frontier grew rare.

sentences.zh: 今紛爭，正不當問，奈何殃赤子以威小醜，割心腹以補四肢，無益有害。

translations.literal: Now they are in strife—precisely the time not to intervene; why harm innocent people to overawe petty villains, cutting the heart to patch the limbs, to no profit and much harm?
translations.idiomatic: Their quarrel is precisely when we should stand aside—why scourge the innocent to frighten petty foes, cutting the heart to save a limb, with harm and no gain?

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: Third.
translations.idiomatic: Third.

sentences.zh: 若謂中國近境，宜乘亂取之。

translations.literal: If one says that because it borders China we should seize the disorder to take it,
translations.idiomatic: If one says that because it lies near China we should seize the moment of disorder,

sentences.zh: 臣考馬援南征，深歷浪泊，士卒死亡幾半，所立銅柱為漢極界，乃近在今思明府耳。

translations.literal: I examine Ma Yuan's southern campaign: he penetrated deep to Langbo, and nearly half his soldiers died; the bronze pillar he erected marked the Han frontier, and that was near today's Siming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Ma Yuan's southern campaign: he reached deep into Langbo, lost nearly half his army, and the bronze pillar that marked Han's limit stood near today's Siming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先朝雖嘗平之，然屢服屢叛，中國士馬物故者以數十萬計，竭二十余年之財力，僅得數十郡縣之虛名而止。

translations.literal: Though our dynasty once pacified the region, it repeatedly submitted and repeatedly rebelled; Chinese soldiers and horses who perished number in the hundreds of thousands, and twenty years of state wealth were exhausted—yet we gained only the empty name of several dozen commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty too once pacified it, yet it rebelled again and again; hundreds of thousands of men and horses died and twenty years of revenue were spent—for the hollow title of a few dozen districts.

sentences.zh: 況又有征之不克，如宋太宗、神宗，元憲宗、世祖朝故事乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, there are cases where campaigns did not succeed, as in the reigns of Song Taizong and Shenzong and under the Yuan emperors Xianzong and Shizu—is this not a lesson?
translations.idiomatic: And campaigns failed—as under Song Taizong and Shenzong, and Yuan Xianzong and Shizu—should this not warn us?

sentences.zh: 此可為殷鑒。

translations.literal: This can serve as a mirror for warning.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be our mirror.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: Fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth.

sentences.zh: 外邦入貢，乃彼之利。

translations.literal: When outer states enter tribute, it is to their advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute benefits them, not us.

sentences.zh: 一則奉正朔以威其鄰，一則通貿易以足其國。

translations.literal: On one hand they accept the calendar to overawe their neighbors; on the other they trade to enrich their state.
translations.idiomatic: They accept our calendar to intimidate neighbors and trade to fill their coffers.

sentences.zh: 故今雖兵亂，尚累累奉表箋、具方物，款關求入，守臣以姓名不符卻之。

translations.literal: Therefore even amid warfare today they repeatedly send memorials and local products, knocking at the passes to enter, yet garrison officials reject them because the names do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Even now, amid war, they still send memorials and gifts and beg entry at the passes—yet border officials turn them away over mismatched names.

sentences.zh: 是彼欲貢不得，非抗不貢也。

translations.literal: They wish to offer tribute but cannot—this is not defiance of tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They want to tribute but are refused—not defiance of tribute.

sentences.zh: 以此責之，詞不順。

translations.literal: To blame them on this ground is unjust.
translations.idiomatic: To punish them on this score is unjust.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth.

sentences.zh: 興師則需餉。

translations.literal: To raise troops requires supplies.
translations.idiomatic: War demands provisions.

sentences.zh: 今四川有采木之役，貴州有凱口之師，而兩廣積儲數十萬，率耗於田州岑猛之役。

translations.literal: Sichuan now has timber-cutting corvée, Guizhou has the Kaikou campaign, and the two Guang provinces have stored several hundred thousand piculs, mostly consumed in the campaign against Cen Meng of Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan faces timber corvée, Guizhou the Kaikou campaign, and the two Guang have stored hundreds of thousands of piculs—mostly spent on Cen Meng of Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 又大工頻興，所在軍儲悉輸將作，興師數十萬，何以給之？

translations.literal: Great works arise frequently, and military stores everywhere are poured into the Directorate of Works; with an army of hundreds of thousands, how can it be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Grand projects multiply, military stores drain to the Directorate of Works—how feed an army of hundreds of thousands?

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: Sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth.

sentences.zh: 然臣所憂，又不止此。

translations.literal: Yet what I fear is not limited to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my fears go further still.

sentences.zh: 唐之衰也，自明皇南詔之役始。

translations.literal: The Tang dynasty's decline began with Emperor Minghuang's campaign against Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's fall began with Minghuang's Nanzhao war.

sentences.zh: 宋之衰也，自神宗伐遼之役始。

translations.literal: The Song dynasty's decline began with Emperor Shenzong's campaign against Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Song's fall began with Shenzong's war on Liao.

sentences.zh: 今北寇日強，據我河套。

translations.literal: Today northern enemies grow stronger daily and hold our Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: Northern foes grow stronger and hold our Ordos.

sentences.zh: 邊卒屢叛，毀我藩籬。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers rebel repeatedly and tear down our defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops rebel and breach our defenses.

sentences.zh: 北顧方殷，更啟南征之議，脫有不測，誰任其咎？

translations.literal: With the north still pressing, to open talk of a southern campaign—if mishap follows, who will bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: The north still alarms us—open a southern war, and who answers if disaster strikes?

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: Seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh.

sentences.zh: 錦衣武人，暗於大體。

translations.literal: Brocade-clad guards are military men ignorant of great principles.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade-clad agents are soldiers, blind to statecraft.

sentences.zh: 倘稍枉是非之實，致彼不服，反足損威。

translations.literal: If they slightly distort right and wrong, causing the other side not to submit, it will only damage our prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Distort the facts even slightly and they will not submit—our prestige alone will suffer.

sentences.zh: 即令按問得情，伐之不可，不伐不可，進退無據，何以為謀？

translations.literal: Even if investigation obtains the truth, whether to attack or not to attack—we would have no footing; how could we plan?
translations.idiomatic: Even a fair inquiry leaves us unable to attack or not attack—with no footing, how plan?

sentences.zh: 且今嚴兵待發之詔初下，而征求騷擾之害已形，是憂不在外夷，而在邦域中矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the edict for strict military preparations has only just been issued, yet the harm of levies and disturbances already appears—our worry is not outer barbarians but within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The mobilization edict is barely out, yet levies already torment the people—our peril lies within, not beyond.

sentences.zh: 請停遣勘官，罷一切征調，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg that investigating officials be halted and all levies for war stopped—the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Stop the investigators, halt all war levies—the realm would be blessed.

sentences.zh: 章下兵部，請從其議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Ministry of War, which asked that his proposal be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of War, which endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 得旨，待勘官還更議。

translations.literal: The response was: wait until the investigating officials return and discuss again.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: wait until the investigators return, then decide.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，帝決計征討。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year the emperor resolved on punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The next fourth month the emperor resolved on war.

sentences.zh: 侍郎潘珍、兩廣總督潘旦、巡按御史余光相繼諫，皆不納。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Pan Zhen, Grand Coordinator Pan Dan of the two Guang, and Touring Censor Yu Guang remonstrated in succession, but none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Pan Zhen, Grand Coordinator Pan Dan, and Censor Yu Guang protested in turn—all ignored.

sentences.zh: 後遣毛伯溫往，卒撫降之。

translations.literal: Later Mao Bowen was sent; in the end they were pacified and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen was sent later and they were pacified.

sentences.zh: 郭勛為祖英請配享，胄疏爭。

translations.literal: Guo Xun asked that his ancestor Ying be granted joint sacrifice; Zhou memorialized against it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun sought joint sacrifice for his ancestor Ying; Zhou protested.

sentences.zh: 帝欲祀獻皇帝明堂，配上帝，胄力言不可。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to sacrifice to the Prince of Xing in the Bright Hall, paired with the Supreme Lord, Zhou argued forcefully that this could not be.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to honor the Prince of Xing in the Bright Hall beside the Supreme Lord, Zhou objected fiercely.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下詔獄拷掠，削籍歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, had him imprisoned and tortured under edict, and struck him from the rolls to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, jailed and tortured him, and struck him from office.

sentences.zh: 遇赦復冠帶，卒。

translations.literal: On an amnesty he regained his cap and belt and died.
translations.idiomatic: He regained rank on amnesty and died at home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he was posthumously made right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 胄耿介孝友，好學多著述，立朝有執持，為嶺南人士之冠。

translations.literal: Zhou was upright, filial, and friendly, fond of learning and prolific in writing; in court he held firm views and was foremost among gentlemen of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, filial, and learned, Zhou wrote widely; in court he stood firm and led Lingnan scholars.

sentences.zh: 潘珍，字玉卿，婺源人。

translations.literal: Pan Zhen, styled Yuqing, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhen, whose style was Yuqing, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷官山東僉事，分巡袞州。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period he served as vice commissioner in Shandong, touring Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde he was Shandong vice commissioner, touring Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊劉七等猝至，有備不敢攻，引去，掠曲阜。

translations.literal: When the bandit Liu Qi and others suddenly arrived, because preparations had been made they dared not attack and withdrew, plundering Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Liu Qi came suddenly; finding the city prepared, they spared it but looted Qufu.

sentences.zh: 珍奏徙縣治而城之。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized to move the county seat and wall the town.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen memorialized to relocate the county seat and fortify the walls.

sentences.zh: 遷福建副使，湖廣左布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner in Fujian and left administration commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Fujian vice commissioner, then left administration commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年以右副都御史巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he became right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時議諫討安南，珍上疏諫曰：「陳暠、莫登庸皆殺逆之賊，黎寧與其父譓不請封入貢亦二十年，揆以大義，皆所當討，何獨徇寧請為左右？

translations.literal: When court debated remonstrating against attacking Annam, Zhen memorialized: "Chen Hao and Mo Dengyong are both murderous rebels; Li Ning and his father Kui have not requested enfeoffment or offered tribute for twenty years—by great principle all should be punished. Why favor only Ning's request?
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated war on Annam, Zhen wrote: "Chen Hao and Mo Dengyong are murderers; Li Ning and his father have not sought enfeoffment or tribute for twenty years—all merit punishment by principle. Why heed only Ning?

sentences.zh: 且其地不足郡縣置，叛服無與中國。

translations.literal: Moreover its land is not worth making commanderies and counties; submission and rebellion do not concern China.
translations.idiomatic: Its land is not worth a prefecture; its quarrels are not China's affair.

sentences.zh: 今北敵曰蕃，聯帳萬里，烽警屢聞，顧釋門庭防，遠事瘴蠻，非計之得。

translations.literal: Now northern enemies grow daily, their camps linked for ten thousand li and alarms frequent—yet we would leave our gate undefended to campaign far among miasma barbarians; this is no sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Northern enemies spread for ten thousand li while alarms multiply—yet we would leave the gate open to fight in the south; this is folly.

sentences.zh: 宜遣大臣有文武才者，聲言進討。

translations.literal: We should send a minister with both civil and military talent who proclaims a punitive advance.
translations.idiomatic: Send a minister of civil and military talent who proclaims punishment.

sentences.zh: 檄數登庸罪，赦其脅從，且令黎寧合剿。

translations.literal: Proclaim Dengyong's crimes, pardon those coerced, and order Li Ning to join in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Publish Dengyong's crimes, pardon the coerced, and order Li Ning to join the strike.

sentences.zh: 賊父子不擒則降，何必勞師？」

translations.literal: If father and son are not captured they will submit—why weary the army?"
translations.idiomatic: If they are not taken they will submit—why march an army?

sentences.zh: 帝責珍撓成命，褫職歸。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Zhen for obstructing the settled plan and stripped him of office to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused Zhen of obstructing his decree and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 尋以恩詔復官，致仕。

translations.literal: Soon, on an amnesty edict, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty soon restored his rank; he retired.

sentences.zh: 珍廉直有行誼，中外十余薦，皆報寢。

translations.literal: Zhen was incorrupt and upright with a sense of duty; more than ten recommendations came from inside and outside court, all shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt and upright, he was recommended more than ten times—all ignored.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右都御史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 珍族子旦，字希周。

translations.literal: Zhen's clansman Dan, styled Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's clansman Dan, styled Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 知漳州邵武。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Zhangzhou and Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Zhangzhou and Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 三遷浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to left administration commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose three times to left administration commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 斥羨金不取。

translations.literal: He rejected surplus gold and would not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused surplus tribute gold.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年擢右副都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he was made right vice censor-in-chief and pacification commissioner of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he became right vice censor-in-chief, pacification commissioner of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 數平巨寇。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pacified great bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly suppressed major bandits.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to right vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，以兵部左侍郎提督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year he was made left vice minister of war to supervise military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth winter he became left vice minister of war, supervising the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 詔起復毛伯溫討安南。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Mao Bowen from mourning to campaign against Annam.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Mao Bowen from mourning to attack Annam.

sentences.zh: 旦行過其裏，語之曰：「安南非門庭寇。

translations.literal: As Dan passed through Mao's home district he told him: "Annam is not an enemy at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Mao's home, Dan told him: "Annam is no threshold foe.

sentences.zh: 公宜以終喪辭。

translations.literal: Your Lordship should decline on grounds of unfinished mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Decline on grounds of mourning.

sentences.zh: 往來之間，少緩師期。

translations.literal: In going and coming, delay the campaign slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Delay the march in transit.

sentences.zh: 俟其聞命求款，因撫之，可百全也。」

translations.literal: Wait until they hear the order and seek terms, then pacify them—this can be fully secure.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear the decree and sue for peace, pacify them—then all is safe.

sentences.zh: 旦抵廣，適安南使至，馳疏言：「莫登庸之篡黎氏，猶黎氏之篡陳氏也。

translations.literal: When Dan reached Guang, Annam envoys happened to arrive; he sent an urgent memorial saying: "Mo Dengyong's usurpation of the Li house is like the Li house's usurpation of the Chen house.
translations.idiomatic: At Guang, Annam envoys arrived; Dan memorialized: "Dengyong's seizure of the Li is like Li's seizure of the Chen.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將興問罪師，登庸即有求貢之使，何嘗不畏天威？

translations.literal: The court is about to raise a punitive army, yet Dengyong already has envoys seeking tribute—how can he not fear heavenly majesty?
translations.idiomatic: The court prepares war, yet Dengyong already sends tribute envoys—does he not fear the throne?

sentences.zh: 乞容臣等觀變，待彼國自定。

translations.literal: I beg that your servant be allowed to watch developments and wait until their state settles itself.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to watch and wait until their realm settles.

sentences.zh: 若登庸奉表獻琛，於中國體足矣，豈必窮兵萬里哉。」

translations.literal: If Dengyong presents a memorial and offers gems, that suffices for China's dignity—why must we weary troops for ten thousand li?"
translations.idiomatic: If Dengyong submits memorials and tribute, China's honor is satisfied—why march ten thousand li?"

sentences.zh: 章下禮、兵二部。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Ministries of Rites and War.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to Rites and War.

sentences.zh: 族父珍適以言得罪，尚書嚴嵩、張瓚絀旦議不用。

translations.literal: Zhen, Dan's clansman, had just been punished for his words; Ministers Yan Song and Zhang Zan suppressed Dan's proposal and did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had just been punished; Yan Song and Zhang Zan shelved Dan's plan.

sentences.zh: 會伯溫人都，見旦疏不悅。

translations.literal: When Bowen entered the capital he saw Dan's memorial and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen, reaching the capital, disliked Dan's memorial.

sentences.zh: 言總督任重，宜擇知兵者。

translations.literal: He said the grand coordinator's responsibility was weighty and someone who knew warfare should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: He said the grand coordinator's post required a man who knew war.

sentences.zh: 遂改旦南京兵部，以張經代之。

translations.literal: Dan was therefore transferred to the Ministry of War at Nanjing, and Zhang Jing replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was moved to Nanjing War Ministry; Zhang Jing replaced him.

sentences.zh: 未行，引疾乞休，語侵伯溫。

translations.literal: Before setting out he pleaded illness and asked to retire, his language insulting Bowen.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he begged sick leave and insulted Bowen.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，勒致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to retire in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 將還，吏白例支庫金為道里費。

translations.literal: As he was about to return, clerks reported the precedent of drawing treasury silver for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On departure, clerks offered travel silver from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 旦笑曰：「吾不以妄取為例。」

translations.literal: Dan laughed and said: "I do not take wrongful gain as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Dan laughed: "I do not treat theft as precedent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 旦上書半歲，廣東巡按御史余光亦言：「黎氏魚肉國君，在陳氏為賊子；

translations.literal: Half a year after Dan's memorial, Guangdong touring censor Yu Guang also said: "The Li house oppressed its ruler like fish on the chopping block—in the Chen house they were unfilial sons;
translations.idiomatic: Six months later Guangdong censor Yu Guang wrote: "The Li oppressed their lord—in the Chen line they were parricides;

sentences.zh: 抗拒中國，在我朝為亂魁。

translations.literal: resisting China, in our dynasty they are rebel chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: resisting China, in our dynasty they are rebels.

sentences.zh: 今失國，或天假手登庸以報之也。

translations.literal: Now having lost the state, perhaps Heaven lends Dengyong's hand to repay them.
translations.idiomatic: Now overthrown, perhaps Heaven uses Dengyong to repay them.

sentences.zh: 自宋以來，丁移於李，李奪於陳，陳篡於黎，今黎又轉於莫。

translations.literal: Since the Song, Ding gave way to Li, Li was seized by Chen, Chen was usurped by Li, and now Li has passed to Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song, Ding fell to Li, Li to Chen, Chen to Li, Li to Mo.

sentences.zh: 欲興黎氏，勢必不能。

translations.literal: To revive the Li house would certainly be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Reviving the Li is impossible.

sentences.zh: 臣已遣官責其修貢。

translations.literal: Your servant has already sent officials to demand tribute.
translations.idiomatic: I have already sent officers to demand tribute.

sentences.zh: 道里懸遠，往復陳請，必失事機。

translations.literal: The roads are far and requests back and forth will surely miss the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Distance and repeated memorials will miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 乞令臣便宜從事。」

translations.literal: I beg that your servant be allowed to act as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 帝以光疏中引五季、六朝事，下之兵部。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Guang's memorial cited events of the Five Dynasties and Six Dynasties period, sent it to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting Guang cited Five Dynasties and Six Dynasties parallels, sent the memorial to War.

sentences.zh: 咎光輕率，奪其俸。

translations.literal: He blamed Guang for rashness and docked his salary.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Guang for rashness and cut his pay.

sentences.zh: 無何，光進鄉試錄。

translations.literal: Before long, Guang submitted the provincial examination roster.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guang submitted the provincial examination roster.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書嚴嵩摘其誤，奏之，被逮削籍。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yan Song picked out errors and memorialized; Guang was arrested and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song found errors and had Guang arrested and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 光，江寧人。

translations.literal: Guang was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Guang came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 李中，字子庸，吉水人，正德九年進士。

translations.literal: Li Zhong, styled Ziyong, was a native of Jishui and passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong, styled Ziyong, from Jishui, passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 楊一清為吏部，數召中應言官試，不赴。

translations.literal: When Yang Yiqing was minister of personnel he repeatedly summoned Zhong to the censorial examination, but Zhong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing as personnel minister repeatedly tested Zhong for censorial office; Zhong refused.

sentences.zh: 及授工部主事，武宗自稱大慶法王，建寺西華門內，用番僧住持，廷臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: After he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works, the Martial Emperor styled himself the Daqing Dharma King, built a temple inside Xihua Gate, and installed Tibetan monks as abbots—court ministers dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: As a Works secretary, the Martial Emperor styled himself Daqing Dharma King, built a temple inside Xihua Gate with Tibetan abbots—and ministers were silent.

sentences.zh: 中拜官三月即抗疏曰：「曩逆瑾竊權，勢焰薰灼。

translations.literal: Three months after taking office Zhong submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Formerly the rebel Jin usurped power and his arrogance scorched all.
translations.idiomatic: Three months in office Zhong memorialized boldly: "Once Jin usurped power and scorched the court.

sentences.zh: 陛下既悟，誅之無赦，聖武可謂卓絕矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty understood, executed him without mercy—sagely martial prowess can be called surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw through him and executed him without mercy—sagely martial indeed.

sentences.zh: 今大權未收，儲位未建，義子未革，紀綱日馳，風俗日壤，小人日進，君子日退，士氣日靡，言路日閉，名器日輕，賄賂日行，禮樂日廢，刑罰日濫，民財日殫，軍政日弊。

translations.literal: Today great power is not gathered back, the heir is not established, adopted sons are not abolished; statutes daily slip, customs daily decay, petty men daily advance and gentlemen daily retreat, morale daily falters, the avenue of speech daily closes, honors daily cheapen, bribery daily spreads, rites and music daily fall into ruin, punishments daily run wild, the people's wealth daily exhausts, and military government daily deteriorates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet power is not gathered, the heir unset, adopted sons unreformed; law slips, morals rot, flatterers rise and gentlemen fall, morale sinks, speech is sealed, honors cheapen, bribery spreads, rites decay, punishments run wild, wealth drains, and the army rots.

sentences.zh: 瑾既誅矣，而善治一無可舉者，由陛下惑異端故也。

translations.literal: Jin is already executed, yet no good governance can be undertaken—this is because Your Majesty is deluded by heterodox teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Jin is dead, yet no good rule appears—because Your Majesty is lost in heterodox ways.

sentences.zh: 夫禁掖嚴邃，豈異教所得雜居？

translations.literal: The inner palace is stern and secluded—how can heterodox teachings be allowed to mingle there?
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace is deeply guarded—how can foreign faiths be allowed to live there?

sentences.zh: 今乃建寺西華門內，延止番僧，日與聚處。

translations.literal: Now a temple is built inside Xihua Gate, Tibetan monks are invited to stay, and they gather together daily.
translations.idiomatic: A temple has been built inside Xihua Gate, Tibetan monks lodged there, meeting daily.

sentences.zh: 異言日沃，忠言日遠，用舍顛倒，舉錯乖方。

translations.literal: Foreign speech daily pours in, loyal speech daily recedes; appointments and dismissals are inverted, and actions miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Alien counsel floods in while loyal words fade; the wrong men rise, actions go awry.

sentences.zh: 政務廢馳，職此之故。

translations.literal: Government affairs are neglected and slip away—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: State business lies abandoned—for this reason.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下翻然悔悟，毀佛寺，出番僧，妙選儒臣，朝夕勸講，攬大權以絕天下之奸，建儲位以立天下之本，革義子以正天下之名，則所謂振紀綱、勵風俗、進君子、退小人諸事，可次第舉矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will suddenly repent, destroy Buddhist temples, expel Tibetan monks, carefully select Confucian officials for daily counsel, gather great power to cut off treachery under heaven, establish an heir to fix the foundation under heaven, and abolish adopted sons to correct names under heaven; then what is called restoring discipline, reforming custom, advancing gentlemen and retiring petty men can be carried out step by step.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will repent, tear down the temples, send the monks away, choose fine Confucian counselors for daily instruction, seize power to root out treason, name an heir to secure the realm, and end adopted-son titles to set the court right—then restoring law, reforming manners, promoting the worthy and dismissing the base can follow in order.

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 罪將不測，以大臣救得免。

translations.literal: Punishment was immeasurable, but he was spared through a minister's intercession.
translations.idiomatic: He faced unknown punishment but was spared when a senior minister intervened.

sentences.zh: 逾日，中旨謫廣東通衢驛丞。

translations.literal: The next day an imperial order demoted him to assistant at Tongqu Post in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Next day an imperial edict banished him to Tongqu Post station in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 王守仁撫贛州，檄中參其軍事。

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren pacified Ganzhou, he summoned Zhong through an official dispatch to serve on his military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, pacifying Ganzhou, called Zhong by dispatch to his staff.

sentences.zh: 預平宸濠。

translations.literal: He took part in suppressing Prince Chen Hao's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Prince Chen Hao's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，復故官。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Zhong was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's accession Zhong was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 未任，擢廣東僉事。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before assuming it he was made Guangdong vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再遷廣西提學副使，以身為教。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Guangxi vice commissioner for education and taught by personal example.
translations.idiomatic: Then as Guangxi education vice commissioner he taught by example.

sentences.zh: 擇諸生高等聚五經書院，五日一登堂講難。

translations.literal: He selected the top students and gathered them at the Five Classics Academy, lecturing and debating once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the best students at the Five Classics Academy for debate lectures every five days.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣東右布政使。

translations.literal: On a third transfer he became right administrative commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: A third promotion made him Guangdong right administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 忤總督及巡撫御史，坐以不稱職，當罷。

translations.literal: He offended the grand coordinator and the censor-in-chief, was charged with incompetence, and was due to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the governor and touring censor, was found unfit, and marked for removal.

sentences.zh: 霍韜署吏部事，稱中素廉節有才望，當留。

translations.literal: Huo Tao, acting for the Ministry of Personnel, praised Zhong's lifelong integrity and talent and said he should be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao at Personnel praised Zhong's integrity and talent and argued he should stay.

sentences.zh: 會政府有不悅者，降四川右參政。

translations.literal: As there were those in government who disliked him, he was demoted to right vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies in court lowered him to Sichuan right vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年擢右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he became right assistant censor-in-chief and Shandong coordinator.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，令民捕蝗者倍予谷，蝗絕而饑者濟。

translations.literal: In a lean year he ordered that grain be doubled for those who caught locusts; when locusts were gone the hungry were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he doubled grain pay for locust hunters; when the swarms ended the hungry were fed.

sentences.zh: 擒劇盜關繼光，鄰境攘其功，中不與辯。

translations.literal: He captured the notorious bandit Guan Jiguang; a neighboring jurisdiction seized the credit, but Zhong did not dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: He caught the bandit Guan Jiguang; neighbors claimed the credit and he did not argue.

sentences.zh: 進副都御史，總督南京糧儲。

translations.literal: He advanced to vice censor-in-chief and grand secretary of Nanjing grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice censor-in-chief, he took charge of Nanjing grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 御史金燦按四川時，嘗薦中。

translations.literal: When Censor Jin Can toured Sichuan he had once recommended Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jin Can had recommended Zhong while inspecting Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 中不謝，燦憾之，至是摭他事誣劾。

translations.literal: Zhong did not thank him; Jin resented this and now fabricated charges from other matters to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong never thanked him; Jin now trumped up charges.

sentences.zh: 方議調用而中卒。

translations.literal: Just as transfer was under discussion Zhong died.
