translations.idiomatic: While reassignment was debated, Zhong died.

sentences.zh: 光宗時，追諡莊介。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Guangzong he was posthumously given the posthumous name Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong posthumously named him Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 中守官廉。

translations.literal: Zhong held office with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong served with scrupulous honesty.

sentences.zh: 自廣西歸，欲飯客，貸米鄰家。

translations.literal: Returning from Guangxi he wished to feed guests and borrowed rice from a neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: Back from Guangxi he wanted to entertain guests and borrowed rice next door.

sentences.zh: 米至，又乏薪，將以浴器爨。

translations.literal: When the rice arrived he still lacked fuel and was about to cook with a bath basin.
translations.idiomatic: Rice came but he had no firewood and meant to cook in a bathing tub.

sentences.zh: 會日已暮，竟不及飯而別。

translations.literal: It happened to be evening and in the end the meal never came and the guests departed.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell before dinner; the guests left unfed.

sentences.zh: 少學於同里楊珠，既而擴充之，沈潛邃密，學者稱谷平先生。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under fellow townsman Yang Zhu, then expanded upon it with deep, dense learning; scholars called him Master Guping.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Yang Zhu of his home district, then deepened it into profound learning; scholars called him Master Guping.

sentences.zh: 門人羅洪先、王龜年、周子恭皆能傳其學。

translations.literal: Disciples Luo Hongxian, Wang Guinian, and Zhou Zigong all could transmit his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples Luo Hongxian, Wang Guinian, and Zhou Zigong carried on his teachings.

sentences.zh: 中族人楷，又傳洪先之學。

translations.literal: Zhong's clansman Kai also transmitted Hongxian's learning.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Kai also passed on Hongxian's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 楷，字邦正。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Bangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Bangzheng.

sentences.zh: 由舉人授湯溪知縣。

translations.literal: Through the provincial graduate degree he was appointed magistrate of Tangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he became magistrate of Tangxi.

sentences.zh: 母艱服闋，補靑田。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother ended he was reassigned to Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he was posted to Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 時倭躪東南，楷積谷資守禦。

translations.literal: At that time Japanese pirates ravaged the southeast; Kai stockpiled grain to support defense.
translations.idiomatic: As pirates ravaged the southeast he hoarded grain for defense.

sentences.zh: 靑田故無城。

translations.literal: Qingtian originally had no wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtian had never had walls.

sentences.zh: 倭至，楷禦於沙埠，倭不得渡，乃以間築城。

translations.literal: When pirates arrived Kai held them at Shabu; they could not cross, and he used the interval to build a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders came he blocked them at Shabu; unable to cross, he used the lull to build walls.

sentences.zh: 倭又至，登陴守，日殺賊數人，倭遁去。

translations.literal: When pirates came again he mounted the ramparts to defend, killing several raiders each day until they fled.
translations.idiomatic: They returned; he held the walls, killing several each day until they fled.

sentences.zh: 改知昌樂，亦以治行聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Changle and was also known for effective governance.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Changle, he won fame for good rule.

sentences.zh: 歐陽鐸，字崇道，泰和人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Duo, courtesy name Chongdao, a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Duo, styled Chongdao, was from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: Made a courier.

sentences.zh: 上書極論時政，不報。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial vigorously discussing current policy and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized boldly on policy; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 使蜀府，王厚遺之，不受。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Shu princely establishment, Wang Hou gave him gifts and he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy to the Shu prince, he refused rich gifts from Wang Hou.

sentences.zh: 歷工部郎中，改南兵部。

translations.literal: He served as a director in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Works, then moved to Nanjing War.

sentences.zh: 出為延平知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Yanping prefect.

sentences.zh: 毀淫祠數十百所，以其材葺學宮。

translations.literal: He destroyed dozens or hundreds of illicit shrines and used their timber to repair the school.
translations.idiomatic: He razed scores of illicit shrines and rebuilt the academy with their timber.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監蕭敬家奴殺人，置之法。

translations.literal: A household slave of eunuch-director Xiao Jing killed a man; Duo had him punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jing's slave committed murder, Duo had him executed.

sentences.zh: 調福州，議均徭曰：「郡多士大夫，其士大夫又多田產。

translations.literal: Transferred to Fuzhou, discussing equalized corvée he said: "The prefecture has many scholar-officials, and those scholar-officials hold much land.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fuzhou, debating corvée reform he said: "The prefecture has many gentry, and the gentry hold most of the land.

sentences.zh: 民有產者無幾耳，而徭則盡責之民。

translations.literal: Common people with property are few, yet corvée is loaded entirely on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Few commoners own land, yet all corvée falls on them.

sentences.zh: 請分民半役。」

translations.literal: I ask that the people bear half the service.
translations.idiomatic: Let commoners bear only half the burden.

sentences.zh: 士大夫率不便。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials generally found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry mostly objected.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史汪珊力持之，議乃行。

translations.literal: Touring censor Wang Shan strongly upheld it, and the proposal was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Shan enforced it, and the plan took effect.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年擢廣東提學副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner for education.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year three made him Guangdong education vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京光祿卿，歷右副都御史，巡撫應天十府。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to Nanjing director of the Imperial Household, then served as right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinating the ten prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Nanjing Household director, then right vice censor coordinating Yingtian's ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松田不甚相懸。

translations.literal: Fields in Suzhou and Songjiang did not differ greatly in quality.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Songjiang fields were not far apart in quality.

sentences.zh: 下者畝五升，上者至二十倍。

translations.literal: Low-grade plots yielded five sheng per mu, high-grade up to twenty times as much.
translations.idiomatic: Poor plots yielded five sheng per mu; rich ones up to twenty times more.

sentences.zh: 鐸令賦最重者減耗米，派輕賫；

translations.literal: Duo ordered that the heaviest assessments reduce transportation-loss grain and assign lighter surcharges;
translations.idiomatic: Duo cut loss-grain surcharges on the heaviest assessments and shifted lighter fees;

sentences.zh: 最輕者征本色，增耗米。

translations.literal: the lightest assessments were collected in kind with added transportation-loss grain.
translations.idiomatic: the lightest plots paid in kind with added loss-grain.

sentences.zh: 陰輕重之，賦乃均。

translations.literal: Thus light and heavy were secretly balanced and the levies evened.
translations.idiomatic: By shifting weight secretly he equalized the levies.

sentences.zh: 諸推收田，從圩不從戶，詭寄無所容。

translations.literal: For all land registered for collection, reckoning followed polder boundaries not households, leaving no room for fraudulent registration.
translations.idiomatic: Tax rolls followed field boundaries not households, blocking false registration.

sentences.zh: 州縣荒田四千四百余頃，歲勒民償賦。

translations.literal: Four thousand four hundred-odd qing of wasteland in prefectures and counties forced the people yearly to pay tax.
translations.idiomatic: Over 4,400 qing of wasteland still taxed the people each year.

sentences.zh: 鐸以所清漏賦及他奇羨補之。

translations.literal: Duo used recovered hidden levies and other surplus revenue to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Duo covered it from recovered hidden taxes and other surpluses.

sentences.zh: 議徭役及裁郵置費凡數十百條，民皆稱便。

translations.literal: He drafted dozens or hundreds of proposals on corvée and cutting courier expenses; the people all called them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Scores of reforms on corvée and post fees won universal praise.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部侍郎，進吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of war at Nanjing and advanced to right vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Made Nanjing vice war minister, then right vice personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳去。

translations.literal: When the nine ancestral temples burned he submitted his own resignation.
translations.idiomatic: After the nine temples burned he resigned on his own account.

sentences.zh: 鐸有文學，內行修潔。

translations.literal: Duo had literary talent and refined personal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was learned and upright in private life.

sentences.zh: 仕雖通顯，家具蕭然。

translations.literal: Though his official career was prominent, his furnishings were bare.
translations.idiomatic: For all his rank, his home was bare.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，諡恭簡。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made minister of works and given the posthumous name Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously minister of works, posthumous name Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 陶諧，字世和，會稽人。

translations.literal: Tao Xie, courtesy name Shihe, a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Xie, styled Shihe, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: First place in the provincial examination in the eighth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Top provincial candidate, Hongzhi year eight.

sentences.zh: 明年成進士，選庶吉士，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he became a jinshi, was selected a hanlin bachelor, and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Next year a jinshi and hanlin bachelor, made Works supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 請命儒臣日講《大學衍義》，孝宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: He asked that Confucian officials daily lecture on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; Emperor Xiaozong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He urged daily lectures on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; Xiaozong approved.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，劉瑾等亂政。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Zhengde, Liu Jin and others misruled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde began, Liu Jin and his faction misgoverned.

sentences.zh: 諧請以瑾等誤國罪告先帝，罪之勿赦。

translations.literal: Xie asked that Jin and others be charged before the late emperor with the crime of harming the state and punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xie demanded Jin be charged before the late emperor with betraying the realm, unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 瑾摘其譌字令對狀，伏罪乃宥之。

translations.literal: Jin picked out errors in characters and ordered him to answer in court; only after confessing guilt was he pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized on textual errors, forced a confession, then spared him.

sentences.zh: 帝命中官崔杲等往江南、浙江織造，杲等復乞長蘆鹽引。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered eunuchs Cui Gao and others to Jiangnan and Zhejiang for imperial weaving; Gao and others again begged for Changlu salt certificates.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent eunuchs Cui Gao and others to weave in Jiangnan and Zhejiang; they also sought Changlu salt licenses.

sentences.zh: 諧再疏爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Xie memorialized twice in protest and was not heeded either time.
translations.idiomatic: Xie protested twice; both pleas were ignored.

sentences.zh: 諧當出理邊儲，以工科掌印無人，請俟行日遣官代署。

translations.literal: Xie was due to go out to manage frontier granaries; since no one held the Works seal he asked to wait until departure and send an official to act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Bound for frontier granaries, with no one to hold the Works seal he asked an interim appointee until he left.

sentences.zh: 瑾遂中諧，下詔獄廷杖，斥為民。

translations.literal: Jin then trapped Xie, had him imprisoned in the imperial prison and beaten at court, and banished him as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin framed him, had him beaten in the imperial prison, and expelled him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 旋榜為奸黨。

translations.literal: Soon he was posted on the roster of the wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon listed among the wicked faction.

sentences.zh: 又誣以巡視十庫時缺布不奏，復械至闕下杖之，謫戍肅州。

translations.literal: He was further accused that while inspecting the ten storehouses he failed to report a cloth shortage; he was again shackled, brought to court for beating, and exiled to garrison duty at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of hiding a cloth shortage while inspecting the ten storehouses, he was beaten again at court and exiled to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，釋還鄉，其黨猶用事，竟不獲召。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed he was released to return home; Jin's faction still held power and in the end he was never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's death he went home free, but Jin's men still ruled and he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year one restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 未至，除江西僉事，轉河南管河副使。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was appointed Jiangxi vice commissioner and transferred to Henan vice commissioner for river control.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking post he became Jiangxi vice commissioner, then Henan river-control vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 命沿河植柳，傍藝葭葦，有事采以為埽。

translations.literal: He ordered willows planted along the river and reeds cultivated beside them; when needed they were harvested for embankment mats.
translations.idiomatic: He planted willows and reeds along the river for emergency embankment material.

sentences.zh: 總理都御史請推行之諸道，歲省費鉅萬。

translations.literal: The supervising censor-in-chief asked that this be extended to all circuits, saving tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor spread the practice circuit-wide, saving tens of thousands yearly.

sentences.zh: 遷參政，歷左、右布政使，皆在河南。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner and served successively as left and right administrative commissioners, all in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner, he served as Henan left and right administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢右副都御史，提督南、贛、汀、漳軍務。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief supervising military affairs in Nan, Gan, Ting, and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually made right vice censor-in-chief over Nan, Gan, Ting, and Zhang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「守令遷太驟，宜以六年為期。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Prefects and magistrates are transferred too swiftly; a term of six years should be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Prefects and magistrates rotate too fast; fix terms at six years.

sentences.zh: 言官忤旨，當優容。

translations.literal: Censors who offend the throne should be treated with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Censors who cross the throne deserve forbearance.

sentences.zh: 養病官才力堪任者，毋終棄。」

translations.literal: Officials on sick leave whose talent and ability qualify them should not be finally discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Able officials on sick leave should not be cast aside forever.

sentences.zh: 時南京御史馬敭等劾王瓊被逮，而新例養病久者率不復收敘，故諧以為言。

translations.literal: At that time Nanjing censor Ma Yang and others impeached Wang Qiong and were arrested, while under the new rule those on long sick leave were generally not reinstated—hence Xie's remarks.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censors including Ma Yang had been arrested for impeaching Wang Qiong, while long-sick officials were rarely restored—hence Xie's plea.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「今天下差徭煩重。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Today corvée levies under heaven are burdensome and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Corvée levies today are crushing.

sentences.zh: 既有河夫、機兵、打手、富戶、力士諸役，乃編審裏甲，復征曠丁課及供億諸費。

translations.literal: Already there are river laborers, machine soldiers, bravoes, wealthy households, and strongmen services, yet ward registers are still compiled and idle-man taxes and supply expenses are levied again.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond river crews, militia, bravoes, rich-household service, and strongmen, wards were re-registered and idle-man dues and supply fees imposed again.

sentences.zh: 乞皆罷免。」

translations.literal: I beg that all these be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all of this be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝采納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to right vice minister of war grand coordinating military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made right war vice minister, grand coordinator of the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 海寇陳邦瑞、許折桂等突入波羅廟，欲犯廣州，為指揮李筜所蹙。

translations.literal: Sea bandits Chen Bangrui, Xu Zhegui, and others burst into Boluo Temple intending to attack Guangzhou and were pressed by Commander Li Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Sea raiders Chen Bangrui and Xu Zhegui broke into Boluo Temple to strike Guangzhou; Commander Li Dang drove them back.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞投水死，折桂還所執指揮二人，乞就撫。

translations.literal: Bangrui drowned himself; Zhegui returned the two commanders he had seized and begged to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui drowned; Zhegui returned two captured commanders and sought amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諧居折桂等東莞，編為總甲，使約束其黨五百人為新民。

translations.literal: Xie settled Zhegui and others at Dongguan, enrolled them as chief ward heads, and had them restrain five hundred followers as new subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Xie settled Zhegui's band at Dongguan as ward chiefs, binding five hundred men as new subjects.

sentences.zh: 兵部以降賊群聚，恐乘隙為變，令解散其黨。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War, fearing that surrendered bandits massed together might seize an opening to rebel, ordered their followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: War feared the surrendered bandits might rebel and ordered their followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 已，陽春賊趙林花等攻城，與德慶賊鳳二全相倚為患，諧討破百二十五砦。

translations.literal: Later Yangchun bandits Zhao Linhua and others attacked a city, relying on Deqing bandit Feng Erquan as mutual support; Xie attacked and broke one hundred twenty-five stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yangchun bandits led by Zhao Linhua besieged a town with Deqing's Feng Erquan; Xie destroyed 125 stockades.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諧功足錄，第前縱患者誰？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Xie's merit deserves record, but who earlier indulged the troublemakers?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Xie's merit deserves note—but who let the trouble grow?

sentences.zh: 乃僅賚銀幣。

translations.literal: He was given only silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He received only silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 瓊山沙灣洞賊黎佛二等殺典史，諧復剿平。

translations.literal: Qiongshan Shawan Cave bandits Li Fo'er and others killed a registrar; Xie again suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiongshan bandits Li Fo'er and others killed a registrar; Xie crushed them again.

sentences.zh: 為總督三年，俘斬累萬。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator for three years he captured or killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In three years as grand coordinator he captured or killed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was raised to left vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left war vice minister.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳致仕歸。

translations.literal: When the nine ancestral temples burned he submitted his own request to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After the nine temples burned he resigned on his own account.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously minister of war.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was given the posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he was posthumously named Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 孫大順，字景熙。

translations.literal: Sun Dashun, courtesy name Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dashun, styled Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the forty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Jiajing year forty-five.

sentences.zh: 歷官福建右布政使。

translations.literal: He served as right administrative commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Fujian right administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 司帑失銀，吏卒五十人皆坐系。

translations.literal: The treasury lost silver and fifty clerks and runners were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the treasury lost silver, fifty clerks and runners were jailed.

sentences.zh: 大順言於左使曰：「盜者兩三人耳，何盡系之為？

translations.literal: Dashun said to the left commissioner: "The thieves are only two or three people—why imprison them all?
translations.idiomatic: Dashun told the left commissioner: "Only two or three stole it—why jail everyone?

sentences.zh: 請為公治之。」

translations.literal: Allow me to handle it for you.
translations.idiomatic: Let me handle it for you.

sentences.zh: 乃縱囚令跡盜，果得真者。

translations.literal: He then released the prisoners to track the thieves and indeed caught the real culprits.
translations.idiomatic: He freed the prisoners to hunt the thieves and caught the real ones.

sentences.zh: 終右副都御史，廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: He ended as right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Guangxi grand coordinator, right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 弟大臨，字虞臣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dalin, courtesy name Yuchen.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Dalin, styled Yuchen.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing with top honors, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Top jinshi of Jiajing year thirty-five, made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 吳時來劾嚴嵩，大臨為定疏草。

translations.literal: When Wu Shilai impeached Yan Song, Dalin drafted the memorial for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shilai impeached Yan Song, Dalin wrote the draft.

sentences.zh: 時來下詔獄，詰所共謀。

translations.literal: Shilai was imprisoned by imperial order and was questioned about his co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Shilai went to the imperial prison and was asked who else plotted with him.

sentences.zh: 大臨不顧，日餉之藥物，時來亦忍死無一言。

translations.literal: Dalin paid no heed and daily supplied him medicine; Shilai too endured death without a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin ignored the inquiry and daily sent him medicine; Shilai endured torture without naming anyone.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，累官吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Wanli he rose through appointments to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he became vice personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書，謚文僖。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made minister of personnel and given the posthumous name Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously personnel minister, posthumous name Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 大臨少應舉杭州，鄰婦夜奔，拒之，旦遂徙舍。

translations.literal: In youth when taking the examination at Hangzhou, a neighbor's wife came by night and he refused her; at dawn he moved lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: Taking exams at Hangzhou as a youth, he refused a neighbor's wife who came by night and moved out at dawn.

sentences.zh: 為人寬然長者，而內持貞介，不以勢利易。

translations.literal: He was a broad, easygoing elder in manner, yet inwardly held to integrity and did not change for power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly an easy elder, inwardly upright—he never bent to power or profit.

sentences.zh: 大順子允淳，與父同登進士。

translations.literal: Dashun's son Yunchun passed the jinshi examination together with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Dashun's son Yunchun became jinshi alongside his father.

sentences.zh: 終尚寶丞。

translations.literal: He ended as director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Court of Imperial Stud director.

sentences.zh: 潘塤，字伯和，山陽人。

translations.literal: Pan Xun, courtesy name Bohe, a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xun, styled Bohe, was from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Made Works supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 性剛決，彈劾無所避。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute and in impeachment feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and resolute, he feared no one in impeachment.

sentences.zh: 論諸大寮王鼎、劉機、寧杲、陳天祥等，多見納。

translations.literal: He criticized senior officials Wang Ding, Liu Ji, Ning Gao, Chen Tianxiang, and others, and many of his proposals were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached senior officials including Wang Ding, Liu Ji, Ning Gao, and Chen Tianxiang, and many charges stuck.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，塤上疏曰：「陛下蒞阼九年，治效未臻，災祥叠見。

translations.literal: When Qianqing Palace burned, Xun submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has reigned nine years yet good governance has not been achieved and omens and disasters have appeared in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianqing Palace burned, Xun memorialized: "Nine years on the throne, rule still falls short and omens multiply.

sentences.zh: 臣願非安宅不居，非大道不由，非正人不親，非儒術不崇，非大閱不觀兵，非執法不成獄，非骨肉之親不幹政，非汗馬之勞不濫賞。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty dwell only in secure quarters, follow only the great Way, be close only to upright men, honor only Confucian learning, review troops only at grand inspections, pass judgment only through lawful procedure, let no one but kin by blood interfere in government, and grant no reward except for sweat-and-blood merit.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will live only in secure quarters, walk only the great Way, trust only upright men, honor only Confucian learning, review troops only at grand inspections, judge only by law, let only kin by blood govern, and reward only true merit.

sentences.zh: 臣聞陛下好戲謔矣。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that Your Majesty loves jest and banter.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Your Majesty loves jest and banter.

sentences.zh: 臣以為入而內庭琴瑟鐘鼓人倫之樂，不必遊離宮以為歡，狎群小以為快也；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that within the inner court, lutes, zithers, bells, and drums are the music of human relations—there is no need to seek delight in wandering palaces or take pleasure in fawning on petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner court, music and kinship suffice—there is no need for pleasure palaces or petty favorites;

sentences.zh: 出而外廷華裔一統莫非臣妾，不必收朝官為私人，集遠人為勇士也。

translations.literal: outside, the civilized lands under one rule are all your subjects—there is no need to gather court officials as private retainers or assemble foreigners as bravoes.
translations.idiomatic: outside, all the realm is yours—there is no need to keep court officials as private retainers or foreigners as bravoes.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下好佛矣。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that Your Majesty loves Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Your Majesty favors Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 臣以為南郊有天地，太廟有祖宗。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that at the southern altar are Heaven and Earth, and in the Grand Temple are the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern altar stand Heaven and Earth; in the Grand Temple stand the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 錫祉迎庥，佛於何有？

translations.literal: Blessings granted and favor received—what has Buddhism to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Blessings come from Heaven and ancestors—what need of Buddha?

sentences.zh: 番僧可逐而度僧可止也。

translations.literal: Tibetan monks may be expelled and ordination of monks may be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Expel the Tibetan monks and halt new ordinations.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下好勇、好貨、好土木矣。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that Your Majesty loves valor, loves wealth, and loves construction.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Your Majesty loves valor, wealth, and building.

sentences.zh: 臣以為誅奸遏亂，大勇也，不須馳馬試劍以自勞。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that punishing traitors and checking disorder is great valor—there is no need to tire yourself racing horses and testing swords.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing traitors is true valor—no need to race horses and test swords yourself.

sentences.zh: 三軍六師，大武也，不須邊將邊軍以自擁。

translations.literal: The three armies and six hosts are great martial power—there is no need to rely on frontier generals and frontier troops for personal force.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies are the realm's strength—no need for private frontier armies.

sentences.zh: 任土作貢，皇店奚為？

translations.literal: Tribute follows the land's products—what need for imperial shops?
translations.idiomatic: Tribute follows local products—why imperial shops?

sentences.zh: 阛阓駢闐，內市安用？

translations.literal: Markets throng at the city gates—what use for an inner market?
translations.idiomatic: Markets throng outside—why an inner market?

sentences.zh: 阿房壯麗，古以為金塊珠礫也，況養豹乎！

translations.literal: The splendor of Epang was anciently deemed gold blocks and pearl rubble—how much more so keeping leopards!
translations.idiomatic: Epang's splendor was called gold and pearl waste—how much worse to keep leopards!

sentences.zh: 金碧熒煌，古以為塗膏畔血也，況供佛乎！

translations.literal: Glittering gold and jade were anciently deemed grease smeared on fields and blood on boundaries—how much more so supplying Buddha!
translations.idiomatic: Gilded halls were called grease on fields and blood on boundaries—how much worse to supply Buddha!

sentences.zh: 是數者之好皆可已而不已者也。」

translations.literal: These several loves could all be stopped yet are not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these passions could end—but does not.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received; no further answer came.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，上書言：「陛下始者血氣未定，禮度或逾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year he submitted a memorial saying: "At first Your Majesty's vital force was not yet settled and ritual bounds were sometimes overstepped.
translations.idiomatic: In month one of year eleven he wrote: "At first Your Majesty was young and sometimes overstepped ritual bounds.

sentences.zh: 今春秋已盛，更弦易轍，此其時也。

translations.literal: Now spring and autumn are in full strength—it is time to change strings and shift the rut.
translations.idiomatic: Now you are in your prime—it is time to change course.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲居桐，處仁遷義，不失中興。

translations.literal: Formerly Tai Jia dwelt at Tong, moved toward benevolence and righteousness, and did not lose the mid-course restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia once lived at Tong, turned toward benevolence and righteousness, and restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 漢武下輪臺之詔，年已七十，猶為令主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han issued the Luntai edict at age seventy and was still a good ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi issued the Luntai edict at seventy and remained a good ruler.

sentences.zh: 況陛下過未浮於太甲，悔又早於武帝，何愆不可蓋，何治不可建乎？」

translations.literal: How much more so when Your Majesty's faults do not exceed Tai Jia's and your repentance comes earlier than Emperor Wu's—what fault cannot be covered, what governance cannot be established?
translations.idiomatic: Your faults fall short of Tai Jia's and your repentance comes earlier than Wudi's—what fault cannot be mended, what rule cannot be built?

sentences.zh: 時欲毀西安門外民居，有所興作。

translations.literal: At that time the plan was to demolish commoners' houses outside Xi'an Gate for construction.
translations.idiomatic: The court then planned to raze homes outside Xi'an Gate for new building.

sentences.zh: 塤與御史熊相、曹雷復切諫，皆不報。

translations.literal: Xun, together with Censors Xiong Xiang and Cao Lei, remonstrated urgently again, and all received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Censor Xiong Xiang, and Cao Lei protested again; none was heeded.

sentences.zh: 三遷至兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: On a third transfer he became chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: A third promotion made him chief War supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 右都督毛倫以附劉瑾論死，削世蔭。

translations.literal: Right chief commander Mao Lun was sentenced to death for associating with Liu Jin and his hereditary privilege was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Right chief commander Mao Lun was condemned to death for siding with Liu Jin and lost his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 倫嘗有德於錢寧，恃為內援，其子求復襲。

translations.literal: Lun had once shown favor to Qian Ning and relied on him as an inner patron; his son sought restoration of the hereditary title.
translations.idiomatic: Lun had once favored Qian Ning and relied on him at court; his son sought to restore the hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 塤等力爭，寧從中主之，寢其奏。

translations.literal: Xun and others struggled hard against it; Ning intervened from within to support it, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fought it hard; Ning backed it from within and the petition was shelved.

sentences.zh: 忽中旨命塤與吏科給事中呂經各進一階，外調，舉朝大駭。

translations.literal: Suddenly an imperial order promoted Xun and Supervising Secretary Lu Jing of the Bureau of Personnel each one rank and transferred them outside—the whole court was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an imperial order promoted Xun and Personnel supervising secretary Lu Jing one rank each and transferred them out—the court was stunned.

sentences.zh: 給事中邵錫、御史王金等交章請留，不報。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Shao Xi, Censor Wang Jin, and others submitted memorials in succession asking that they be kept, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors petitioned to keep them; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 遂添註塤開州同知。

translations.literal: Xun was then additionally assigned as assistant prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was posted as Kaizhou assistant prefect.

sentences.zh: 嘉請七年，累官右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he rose through appointments to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year seven made him Henan grand coordinator, right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 潞州巨盜陳卿據青陽山為亂，山西巡撫江潮、常道先後討賊無功，乃敕塤會剿。

translations.literal: The great bandit Chen Qing of Luzhou held Qingyang Mountain in rebellion; Henan grand coordinator Jiang Chao and Chang Dao successively attacked the bandits without success, so an edict ordered Xun to join the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou bandit Chen Qing held Qingyang Mountain; coordinators Jiang Chao and Chang Dao failed, and Xun was ordered to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 塤謀於道曰：「賊守險，難以陣。

translations.literal: Xun planned with Dao, saying: "The bandits hold the heights and are hard to meet in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun told Dao: "The bandits hold the heights—hard to fight in formation.

sentences.zh: 合諸路夾攻，出不意奪其險，乃可擒也。」

translations.literal: Unite all routes in pincer attack, seize their strong points by surprise, and then they can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Attack from all sides at once, seize their heights by surprise, and we can capture them.

sentences.zh: 遂分五哨三路入，募土人為導。

translations.literal: They then divided five squads into three routes to enter and hired locals as guides.
translations.idiomatic: They split five squads on three routes and hired local guides.

sentences.zh: 首攻奪井腦，賊悉眾爭險。

translations.literal: First they attacked and seized Jingnao; the bandits mustered all forces to contest the heights.
translations.idiomatic: They first seized Jingnao; the bandits massed to hold the heights.

sentences.zh: 官軍奮擊，大破之，追奔至莎草嶺，毀安陽諸巢。

translations.literal: Government troops fought fiercely and broke them completely, pursued the rout to Shacao Ridge, and destroyed the Anyang nests.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops broke them, pursued to Shacao Ridge, and destroyed the Anyang nests.

sentences.zh: 山東副使牛鸞由潞城入，破賊李莊泉。

translations.literal: Shandong vice commissioner Niu Luan entered through Lucheng and broke the bandits at Lizhuang Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong vice commissioner Niu Luan entered via Lucheng and broke them at Lizhuang Spring.

sentences.zh: 其夕，河南副使翟瓚搗卿巢，卿敗走。

translations.literal: That evening Henan vice commissioner Zhai Zan struck Qing's nest and Qing fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That night Henan vice commissioner Zhai Zan struck Qing's nest and Qing fled.

sentences.zh: 瓚追敗之欒莊山，又敗之神河。

translations.literal: Zan pursued and defeated him at Luanzhuang Mountain and again at Shenhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zan defeated him again at Luanzhuang Mountain and Shenhe.

sentences.zh: 山西僉事陳大綱亦屢蹙賊，先後降二千三百余人。

translations.literal: Shanxi vice commissioner Chen Dagang also repeatedly pressed the bandits; in all two thousand three hundred-odd surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi vice commissioner Chen Dagang also harried them; over 2,300 surrendered in all.

sentences.zh: 自進兵至搜滅賊巢，凡二十九日。

translations.literal: From advancing troops to searching out and destroying the bandit nests, the whole took twenty-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: From the advance to destroying the nests took twenty-nine days.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝將大賚，遣給事中夏言往核，未報。

translations.literal: When victory was reported the Emperor was about to grant great rewards and dispatched Supervising Secretary Xia Yan to verify; no reply had yet come.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reported, the Emperor meant to reward heavily and sent Xia Yan to verify—no answer yet.

sentences.zh: 河南大饑，塤不以時振，而河南知府範璁不待報，輒開倉發粟，民德而頌之。

translations.literal: Henan suffered great famine; Xun did not relieve it in time, while Henan prefect Fan Cong without awaiting report opened the granaries and issued grain—the people were grateful and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Henan famine struck; Xun delayed relief while Prefect Fan Cong opened granaries without waiting—the people praised Fan.

sentences.zh: 塤怨聲大起，流聞禁中。

translations.literal: Resentment against Xun rose loudly and spread to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment against Xun spread to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝切責撫、按匿災狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor sharply rebuked the grand coordinator and censor-in-chief for concealing the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked the coordinator and censor for hiding the famine.

sentences.zh: 塤惶恐引罪，且歸罪於璁，遂為給事中蔡經等所劾。

translations.literal: Xun fearfully confessed guilt and also blamed Fan Cong; he was then impeached by Supervising Secretaries Cai Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xun confessed in fear, blamed Fan Cong, and was impeached by Cai Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 詔罷塤，永不敘用。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Xun and barred him from office forever.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Xun permanently from office.

sentences.zh: 言核上平賊功，塤為首。

translations.literal: When Yan verified and reported the merit in suppressing bandits, Xun was listed first.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's verification ranked Xun first for suppressing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 桂萼惡之，但賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Gui E hated this and granted only silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E blocked full honors and granted only silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 年八十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 呂經，字道夫，陜西寧州人。

translations.literal: Lu Jing, courtesy name Daofu, a native of Ningzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jing, styled Daofu, was from Ningzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Made Rites supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 九年，乾清宮災，經上疏極論義子、番僧、邊帥之害。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Qianqing Palace burned, Jing submitted a memorial vigorously discussing the harm of adopted sons, Tibetan monks, and frontier commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, when Qianqing Palace burned, Jing memorialized against adopted sons, Tibetan monks, and frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 屢遷吏科都給事中，復極論馬昂女弟入宮事，又劾方面最貪暴者四人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel, again vigorously discussed the matter of Ma Ang's younger sister entering the palace, and also impeached the four most greedy and violent regional officials.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to chief Personnel supervising secretary, he again protested Ma Ang's sister entering the palace and impeached the four greediest regional officials.

sentences.zh: 群小鹹惡，遂謫蒲州同知。

translations.literal: Petty men all hated him and he was demoted to assistant prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court favorites hated him and he was demoted to Puzhou assistant prefect.

sentences.zh: 又以事忤中官黃玉，誣劾系獄。

translations.literal: He again offended eunuch Huang Yu, who fabricated charges to impeach him and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He again crossed eunuch Huang Yu, who framed him and had him jailed.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，擢山東參政。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne he was promoted to vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's accession he became Shandong vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年累官右副都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he rose through appointments to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year thirteen made him Liaodong grand coordinator, right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 故事，每軍一，佐以余丁三；

translations.literal: By precedent, for each soldier one, three surplus men were assigned as support;
translations.idiomatic: By custom each soldier had three support men;

sentences.zh: 每馬一，給牧地五十畝。

translations.literal: for each horse one, fifty mu of pasture were granted.
translations.idiomatic: each horse had fifty mu of pasture.

sentences.zh: 經損余丁之二編入均徭冊，盡收牧地還官。

translations.literal: Jing reduced two-thirds of the surplus men and entered them in the corvée register, and reclaimed all pasture land to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cut two-thirds of the support men into the corvée rolls and reclaimed all pasture to the state.

sentences.zh: 又役軍築邊墻，督趣過當。

translations.literal: He also conscripted soldiers to build the frontier wall and drove them beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He also forced soldiers to build the frontier wall and drove them too hard.

sentences.zh: 諸軍詣經乞罷役，都指揮劉尚德叱之不退，經呼左右榜訴者。

translations.literal: The troops went to Jing begging to be released from labor; Chief Commander Liu Shangde shouted at them but they would not withdraw, and Jing called attendants to beat the petitioners.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers begged Jing to end the labor; Commander Liu Shangde shouted them down, and Jing had the petitioners beaten.

sentences.zh: 卒遂爭毆尚德，經竄苑馬寺幽室中。

translations.literal: The soldiers then brawled with Shangde, and Jing fled into a secluded room at the Stud Farm Office.
translations.idiomatic: The men brawled with Shangde; Jing hid in a Stud Farm Office back room.

sentences.zh: 亂卒毀府門，火均徭冊，搜得經，裂其冠裳，幽之都司署。

translations.literal: The mutineers smashed the government gate, burned the corvée register, found Jing, tore his cap and robe, and confined him at the regional commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Mutineers smashed the yamen gate, burned the corvée register, seized Jing, stripped his robes, and held him at the regional command.

sentences.zh: 帝詔經還朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Jing to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Jing back to court.

sentences.zh: 都指揮袁璘將克諸軍草價為辦裝，卒復執經，裸而置之獄，虐辱之，脅鎮守中官王純等奏經十一罪。

translations.literal: Chief Commander Yuan Lin was about to withhold fodder money from the troops to pay for Jing's travel expenses; the soldiers again seized Jing, stripped him naked and put him in prison, abused and humiliated him, and coerced frontier eunuch Wang Chun and others to memorialize eleven charges against Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yuan Lin meant to withhold fodder pay for Jing's travel; the mutineers seized Jing again, stripped and jailed him, abused him, and forced eunuch Wang Chun to list eleven charges.

sentences.zh: 帝逮經。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Jing arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Jing arrested.

sentences.zh: 亂卒復置官校於獄，久之始解。

translations.literal: The mutineers again placed court officers in prison; only after a long time were they released.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers jailed court officers too; they were freed only after a long while.

sentences.zh: 經下詔獄，謫戍茂州。

translations.literal: Jing was sent to the imperial prison and exiled to garrison duty at Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing went to the imperial prison and was exiled to Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 數年釋還。

translations.literal: After several years he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was freed.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，卒。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was restored to office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he was restored to office and died.

sentences.zh: 亂卒為曾銑所定，見《銑傳》。

translations.literal: The mutineers were suppressed by Zeng Xuan—see the biography of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers were put down by Zeng Xuan—see his biography.

sentences.zh: 歐陽重，字子重，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Zhong, courtesy name Zizhong, a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Zhong, styled Zizhong, was from Luling.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 殿試對策，歷詆闕政。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he answered the policy question by denouncing court failings one by one.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace exam he denounced court failings point by point.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Justice secretary.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾兄死，百官往吊，重不往。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin's elder brother died, all officials went to mourn; Zhong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin's brother died, officials mourned; Zhong refused.

sentences.zh: 張銳、錢寧掌廠衛，連構搢紳獄，重皆力與爭。

translations.literal: Zhang Rui and Qian Ning controlled the Brocade Guard and repeatedly framed gentry in prison cases; Zhong struggled hard against them each time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rui and Qian Ning ran the secret police and framed officials; Zhong fought them each time.

sentences.zh: 銳等假他事系之獄，贖杖還職，仍停俸。

translations.literal: Rui and others imprisoned him on other charges; he redeemed the beating and returned to office but salary was still withheld.
translations.idiomatic: They jailed him on other charges; he paid a fine, returned to office, but salary stayed cut.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to director.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 歷四川、雲南提學副使。

translations.literal: He served as vice commissioner for education in Sichuan and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as education vice commissioner in Sichuan and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江按察使，未上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to intendant of Zhejiang but had not yet reported.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang intendant, he had not yet reported.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年春拜右僉都御史，巡撫應天。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year of Jiajing he was appointed right assistant censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of Jiajing year six made him Yingtian grand coordinator, right assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 會尋甸土酋安銓、鳳朝文反，廷議以重諳滇事，乃改雲南。

translations.literal: As Xundian native chieftain An Quan and Feng Chaowen rebelled, the court decided that Zhong knew Yunnan affairs and changed his assignment to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xundian chiefs An Quan and Feng Chaowen rebelled, the court sent Zhong to Yunnan for his local knowledge.

sentences.zh: 初，武定土知府鳳詔母子坐事留雲南，朝文紿其眾，言詔已戮，官軍將盡滅其部黨，以故諸蠻悉從為亂，攻圍會城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wuding native prefect Feng Zhao and his mother had been detained in Yunnan for offenses; Chaowen deceived their followers, saying Zhao had been executed and government troops would exterminate their whole band—hence the tribes all followed in revolt and besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wuding prefect Feng Zhao and his mother had been detained in Yunnan; Chaowen lied that Zhao was dead and troops would wipe out their band, so the tribes rebelled and besieged the capital.

sentences.zh: 重督兵擊敗之，而遣詔母子還故地。

translations.literal: Zhong led troops to defeat them and sent Zhao and his mother back to their former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong defeated them and sent Zhao and his mother home.

sentences.zh: 其黨愕，相率歸之。

translations.literal: Their followers were astonished and returned to them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers, astonished, returned in droves.

sentences.zh: 朝文計窮，絕普渡河走。

translations.literal: Chaowen, at his wit's end, crossed the Pudu River and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chaowen, desperate, fled across the Pudu River.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，殲焉。

translations.literal: Pursuing troops arrived and annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers caught and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 銓逃尋甸故巢。

translations.literal: Quan fled to his old nest in Xundian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan fled to his old Xundian stronghold.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻破其砦，執銓，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Government troops broke his stockade and captured Quan; the bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops stormed his stockade, captured Quan, and ended the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乃散其黨二萬人，遷尋甸府於鳳梧山下，更設守禦千戶所。

translations.literal: They then dispersed twenty thousand followers, moved Xundian prefecture below Fengwu Mountain, and established a new defense garrison.
translations.idiomatic: They dispersed twenty thousand followers, moved Xundian prefecture below Fengwu Mountain, and set up a defense garrison.

sentences.zh: 重推功於前撫臣傅習，並進秩任子。

translations.literal: Zhong credited the merit to former grand coordinator Fu Xi and both were promoted in rank with sons granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong gave credit to former coordinator Fu Xi; both were promoted and sons granted office.

sentences.zh: 緬甸、木邦、隴川、孟密、孟養諸酋相仇殺，各訐奏於朝，下重等勘覆。

translations.literal: Chiefs of Burma, Mong Yang, Longchuan, Meng Mi, and Meng Yang mutually killed and impeached one another at court; the court ordered Zhong and others to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Burma, Mong Yang, Longchuan, Meng Mi, and Meng Yang chiefs feuded and sued one another at court; Zhong was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 遣參政王汝舟、知府嚴時泰等遍歷諸蠻，譬以禍福。

translations.literal: He dispatched Vice Commissioner Wang Ruzhou, Prefect Yan Shitai, and others to visit all the tribes and warn them of fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Commissioner Wang Ruzhou, Prefect Yan Shitai, and others among the tribes to warn them of consequences.

sentences.zh: 皆還侵地，供貢如故。

translations.literal: All returned seized lands and resumed tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: All returned seized lands and resumed tribute.

sentences.zh: 重列善後數事，悉報可，賜璽書褒諭。

translations.literal: Zhong listed several follow-up measures; all were approved and he was granted an imperial seal-letter of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong proposed follow-up measures; all were approved and he received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 重乃恤創殘，振貧乏，輕徭賦，規畫鹽鐵商稅、屯田諸務。

translations.literal: Zhong then relieved the wounded and destitute, aided the poor, lightened corvée and taxes, and planned salt, iron, commercial taxes, and garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then relieved the wounded and poor, cut taxes and corvée, and reorganized salt, iron, trade taxes, and garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 民咸便之。

translations.literal: The people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 雲南歲貢金千兩，費不貲。

translations.literal: Yunnan's annual tribute of gold was one thousand taels and the cost was immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's annual gold tribute of one thousand taels cost a fortune.

sentences.zh: 大理太和蒼山產奇石，鎮守中官遣軍匠攻鑿。

translations.literal: Cangshan in Dali Taihe produced strange stones; the frontier eunuch sent soldiers and artisans to quarry them.
translations.idiomatic: Cangshan in Dali produced strange stones; the frontier eunuch sent soldiers and artisans to quarry them.

sentences.zh: 山崩，壓死無算。

translations.literal: The mountain collapsed and countless were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain collapsed and countless workers died.

sentences.zh: 重皆疏罷之，浮費大省。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized to stop all this and extraneous expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong stopped it all by memorial and cut waste sharply.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鎮守太監杜唐、黔國公沐紹勛相比為奸利，長吏不敢問，群盜由此起。

translations.literal: At that time frontier eunuch Du Tang and Duke of Qian State Mu Shaoxun colluded for illicit profit; senior officials dared not inquire, and bandits arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier eunuch Du Tang and Duke Mu Shaoxun colluded for profit; officials dared not act, and banditry spread.

sentences.zh: 重疏言：盜率唐、紹勛莊戶，請究主者。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized: bandits mostly came from Tang's and Shaoxun's estate tenants—please investigate the masters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong wrote: bandits were mostly tenants of Tang and Shaoxun—investigate their masters.

sentences.zh: 又奏紹勛任千戶何經廣誘奸人，奪民產；

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Shaoxun's commander He Jingguang lured ruffians and seized people's property;
translations.idiomatic: He also charged Shaoxun's commander He Jingguang with luring ruffians and seizing property;

sentences.zh: 唐役占官軍，歲取財萬計。

translations.literal: Tang conscripted official soldiers and took tens of thousands in wealth each year.
translations.idiomatic: Tang conscripted soldiers and took tens of thousands yearly.

sentences.zh: 因極言鎮守中官宜革。

translations.literal: He therefore strongly argued that frontier eunuchs should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He argued strongly to abolish frontier eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 帝頗納其言，頻下詔飭紹勛，命唐還京待勘。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely accepted his words, repeatedly issued edicts to admonish Shaoxun, and ordered Tang back to the capital pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor largely agreed, admonished Shaoxun, and recalled Tang for investigation.

sentences.zh: 二人懼且怒，遣人結張璁，謀去重。

translations.literal: The two feared and grew angry, sent men to ally with Zhang Cong, and plotted to remove Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The two, fearful and angry, allied with Zhang Cong to remove Zhong.

sentences.zh: 會重奉命清異姓冒軍弊，都司久未報，給餉後期。

translations.literal: As Zhong was ordered to purge false registration of non-clan soldiers, the regional command long failed to report and pay was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhong purged false military registration, the regional command delayed reports and pay.

sentences.zh: 唐等遂嗾六衛軍嘩於軍門。

translations.literal: Tang and others then incited the six guard armies to riot at the military gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang incited six guard armies to riot at the military gate.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史劉臬以聞。

translations.literal: Touring censor Liu Nie reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Liu Nie reported it.

sentences.zh: 劾重及唐、紹勛處置失當。

translations.literal: He impeached Zhong and Tang and Shaoxun for mishandling the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhong, Tang, and Shaoxun for mishandling it.

sentences.zh: 璁從中主之，解重職，責臬黨庇，調外任，唐、紹勛不問。

translations.literal: Cong intervened from within to support this; Zhong was removed from office, Nie was charged with partiality and transferred outside, and Tang and Shaoxun went unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Cong backed the ruling; Zhong was removed, Nie was punished for partiality and transferred out, and Tang and Shaoxun went free.

sentences.zh: 都給事中夏言等抗章曰：「以軍士噪罪撫、按，紀綱謂何？

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Xia Yan and others submitted forceful memorials saying: "To punish the grand coordinator and censor because soldiers made a clamor—what becomes of discipline?
translations.idiomatic: Chief supervising secretary Xia Yan protested: "Punishing the coordinator and censor because soldiers rioted—what becomes of discipline?

sentences.zh: 況重奉詔非生事。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhong was acting under imperial order and not creating trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhong acted under imperial order, not on his own.

sentences.zh: 臬言唐、紹勛罪與重等，今處分失宜，無以服天下。

translations.literal: Nie said Tang's and Shaoxun's crimes equaled Zhong's, yet the disposition was improper and cannot satisfy the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Nie said Tang and Shaoxun were equally guilty, yet the ruling satisfies no one.

sentences.zh: 頃年士卒驕悍，相效成風，類以月糧借口。

translations.literal: In recent years soldiers have grown arrogant and fierce, copying one another until it became custom, often using monthly rations as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Lately soldiers have grown bold and copy one another, often using pay as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 如甘肅、大同、福州、保定，事變屢見。

translations.literal: At Gansu, Datong, Fuzhou, and Baoding, disturbances have repeatedly appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu, Datong, Fuzhou, and Baoding have seen repeated mutinies.

sentences.zh: 失今不治，他日當事之臣以此為諱，專務姑息，孰肯為陛下任事哉！

translations.literal: If this is not corrected now, future officials will take it as taboo and specialize in indulgence—who will dare serve Your Majesty faithfully?
translations.idiomatic: If this stands, future officials will only indulge—who will serve Your Majesty faithfully?

sentences.zh: 願曲宥二臣，全朝廷之體。」

translations.literal: I beg leniency for the two officials to preserve the dignity of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Spare the two officials to preserve the court's dignity.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪言等俸。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and stripped Yan and others of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and cut Yan's salary.

sentences.zh: 重罷歸在道，聞御史王化劾其為桂萼黨，不勝忿，抗疏陳辨，請錄「大禮」大獄被逐諸臣，而自乞褫職。

translations.literal: Zhong, dismissed and returning on the road, heard that Censor Wang Hua impeached him as a follower of Gui E; unable to bear the rage, he submitted a forceful memorial in self-defense, asking that officials exiled in the Great Rites cases be recorded, and begged to be stripped of office himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed and homeward, Zhong heard Censor Wang Hua call him Gui E's follower; enraged, he defended himself, asked to restore Great Rites exiles, and begged dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又言得紹勛所遣百戶丁鎮私書，知行賄張璁，乞其覆護；

translations.literal: He also said he had obtained a private letter from Shaoxun's commander Ding Zhen showing bribery to Zhang Cong and begging his protection;
translations.idiomatic: He also produced a letter from Shaoxun's commander Ding Zhen bribing Zhang Cong for protection;

sentences.zh: 璁奸佞，不宜在左右。

translations.literal: Cong is treacherous and should not remain at the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Cong is treacherous and should not stay at court.

sentences.zh: 璁疏辨。

translations.literal: Cong submitted a memorial in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cong defended himself.

sentences.zh: 帝以重失職怨望，黜為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor, holding that Zhong resented his dismissal, demoted him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, saying Zhong resented dismissal, reduced him to commoner.

sentences.zh: 重以臬被謫，言等奪俸，皆由己致之，復疏乞重譴代言官罪。

translations.literal: Zhong, because Nie was demoted and Yan and others lost salary—all caused by himself—again memorialized begging severe punishment for himself in place of the censors.
translations.idiomatic: Because Nie was demoted and Yan lost salary through him, Zhong begged harsh punishment for himself instead of the censors.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，以已除名，置不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angrier; since he was already struck from the rolls, the matter was ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angrier; already disgraced, Zhong was ignored.

sentences.zh: 重家居二十余年，言者屢薦，竟不復召。

translations.literal: Zhong lived at home more than twenty years; memorialists repeatedly recommended him but he was never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: At home twenty years he was repeatedly recommended but never recalled.

sentences.zh: 朱裳，字公垂，沙河人。

translations.literal: Zhu Chang, courtesy name Gongchui, a native of Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chang, styled Gongchui, was from Shahe.

sentences.zh: 年十四為諸生，讀書黌舍，躬執爨。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he became a student, reading in the schoolhouse and personally tending the stove.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was a student, studying and cooking for himself.

sentences.zh: 提學御史顧潛俾受學於崔銑。

translations.literal: Education intendant Gu Qian had him study under Cui Min.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Gu Qian placed him under Cui Min.

sentences.zh: 登正德九年進士，擢御史，巡鹽河南。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Zhengde, was promoted to censor, and inspected salt in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Zhengde year nine, he became censor inspecting Henan salt.

sentences.zh: 錢寧遣人牟鹽利，裳禁不予。

translations.literal: Qian Ning sent men to grab salt profits; Chang refused to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning's men sought salt profits; Chang refused.

sentences.zh: 巡按山東。

translations.literal: He toured as censor in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He toured Shandong as censor.

sentences.zh: 前御史王相忤鎮守中官黎監，被誣下詔獄。

translations.literal: Former Censor Wang Xiang had offended frontier eunuch Li Jian and was falsely charged and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Former censor Wang Xiang had offended eunuch Li Jian and was falsely jailed.

sentences.zh: 裳抗疏直相，劾監八罪。

translations.literal: Chang submitted a forceful memorial vindicating Xiang and impeached Jian on eight charges.
translations.idiomatic: Chang vindicated Xiang and impeached Jian on eight counts.

sentences.zh: 帝還自宣府，裳請下罪己詔，新庶政，以結人心。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from Xuanfu, Chang asked that a self-reproach edict be issued and new policies begun to bind people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned from Xuanfu, Chang urged a self-reproach edict and new policies to win hearts.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 山東大水，淹城武、單二城。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered great floods that submerged Wucheng and Shanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong floods submerged Wucheng and Shanxian.

sentences.zh: 以裳言，命相地改築。

translations.literal: On Chang's recommendation, the court ordered new sites chosen and the cities rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: On Chang's advice the court ordered both cities rebuilt on new sites.

sentences.zh: 帝幸南都久，裳極陳小人熒惑之害。

translations.literal: The Emperor long sojourned in the southern capital; Chang strongly set forth the harm of petty men's deluding influence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor lingered in the southern capital; Chang warned of petty men's corrupting influence.

sentences.zh: 出為鞏昌知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Gongchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年舉治行卓異，遷浙江副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was cited for outstanding governance and transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year two he was cited for outstanding rule and made Zhejiang vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 日啜菜羹，妻操井臼，迎父就養。

translations.literal: He daily ate vegetable broth; his wife worked the mortar; he brought his father to live with him.
translations.idiomatic: He ate plain broth daily; his wife ground grain; he brought his father to live with him.

sentences.zh: 同列知其貧，制衣一襲為壽，父亦拒不納。

translations.literal: Colleagues knowing his poverty made him a suit of clothes for his birthday; his father also refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues made him a birthday suit; his father refused it.

sentences.zh: 三遷至浙江左布政使，以右副都御史總理河道，數條上方略。

translations.literal: On a third transfer he became left administrative commissioner of Zhejiang and as right vice censor-in-chief supervised the waterways, submitting many plans to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: A third promotion made him Zhejiang left commissioner; as right vice censor-in-chief he supervised waterways and submitted many plans.

sentences.zh: 外艱歸，久不起。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning for his mother and long did not resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother and long stayed out of office.

sentences.zh: 帝南巡，謁行在，命以故官總理河道。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the south he visited the temporary palace and was ordered to supervise waterways in his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour the Emperor ordered him back to his old waterworks post.

sentences.zh: 迎章聖太后梓宮，冒暑卒。

translations.literal: Receiving Empress Zhangsheng's coffin, he died from heat exposure.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting Empress Zhangsheng's coffin, he died in the heat.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，追贈戶部右侍郎，謚端簡。

translations.literal: In Longqing he was posthumously made right vice minister of revenue and given the posthumous name Duanjian.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing he was posthumously revenue vice minister, posthumous name Duanjian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，按四川。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing he toured as censor in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he inspected Sichuan as censor.

sentences.zh: 請罷鎮守中官，不聽。

translations.literal: He asked that frontier eunuchs be abolished; the request was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to abolish frontier eunuchs; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 帝親鞫楊言，落其一指。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally interrogated Yang Yan and cut off one of his fingers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally tried Yang Yan and cut off a finger.

sentences.zh: 察大呼曰：「臣願以不肖軀易言命，不忍言獨死。」

translations.literal: Cha cried out: "Your servant wishes to exchange his unworthy body for Yan's life—I cannot bear that Yan alone should die.
translations.idiomatic: Cha cried out: "Take my worthless life instead of Yan's—I cannot bear Yan dying alone.

sentences.zh: 帝目攝之，察不為動。

translations.literal: The Emperor glared at him, but Cha did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor glared; Cha did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 退具疏申理，且請下王邦奇於獄，直聲震朝野。

translations.literal: Retiring, he submitted a detailed memorial in defense and also asked that Wang Bangqi be sent to prison; his upright voice shook court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized in Yang's defense and demanded Wang Bangqi be jailed; his bold voice shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 巡視京營，與給事中王科極陳武定侯郭勛貪橫狀。

translations.literal: Inspecting the capital garrison, he and Supervising Secretary Wang Ke strongly set forth the greed and arrogance of Military Marquis Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the capital garrison with Wang Ke, he exposed Marquis Guo Xun's greed and arrogance.

sentences.zh: 擢南京太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Nanjing Court of Imperial Stud vice director.

sentences.zh: 疎辭，因請召前給事中劉世賢等二十餘人。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining and also asked that former Supervising Secretary Liu Shixian and more than twenty others be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and asked to recall former supervising secretary Liu Shixian and twenty others.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責以市恩要名，貶遠方雜職。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, rebuked him for currying favor and seeking fame, and demoted him to a minor post in a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, calling it favor-currying, demoted him to a distant minor post.

sentences.zh: 給事中王俊民、鄭一鵬論救，皆奪俸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wang Junmin and Zheng Yipeng memorialized in his defense; all lost salary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junmin and Zheng Yipeng defended him; all lost salary.

sentences.zh: 察補海陽教諭。

translations.literal: Cha was reassigned as instructor at Haiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was posted as Haiyang instructor.

sentences.zh: 累遷山西左布政使，入為光祿卿。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to left administrative commissioner of Shanxi and entered office as director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Shanxi left commissioner, then Household director.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以僉都御史巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made assistant censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Year twelve made him Nan and Gan grand coordinator, assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 居二年，乞休，因薦前都御史萬鏜、大理卿董天錫等十四人可用。

translations.literal: After two years he begged retirement and recommended fourteen men including former censor-in-chief Wan Yong and chief judge Dong Tianxi as usable.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he retired and recommended fourteen men including Wan Yong and Dong Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 吏部請從其言。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel asked that his words be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel asked to follow his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 帝奪部臣俸，責察徇私妄舉，斥為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor stripped the ministry officials of salary, rebuked Cha for partiality and reckless recommendation, and expelled him as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor cut Personnel's salary, called Cha partial, and expelled him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 察居官廉，既歸，敝衣糲食而已。

translations.literal: Cha held office with integrity; after returning home he had only worn clothes and coarse food.
translations.idiomatic: Cha served with integrity; at home he wore rags and ate plain food.

sentences.zh: 孫懋，字德夫，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Sun Mao, courtesy name Defu, a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mao, styled Defu, was from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received the jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授浦城知縣，擢南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Pucheng and promoted to supervising secretary in the Nanjing Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Pucheng, then Nanjing Personnel supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 御史張經、寧波知府翟唐忤奄人被逮，懋偕同官論救。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Jing and Ningbo prefect Zhai Tang offended eunuchs and were arrested; Mao joined fellow officials in memorializing for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Jing and Ningbo prefect Zhai Tang offended eunuchs and were arrested; Mao joined colleagues in their defense.

sentences.zh: 織造太監史宣誣主事王鑾、知縣胡守約，下之詔獄。

translations.literal: Weaving eunuch Shi Xuan falsely charged Chief Secretary Wang Luan and Magistrate Hu Shouyue and sent them to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving eunuch Shi Xuan framed chief secretary Wang Luan and magistrate Hu Shouyue and jailed them.

sentences.zh: 懋言：「宣妄言禦賜黃棍，聽撻死官吏，脅主簿孫錦死，今又誣守職臣。

translations.literal: Mao said: "Xuan falsely claimed imperial yellow clubs and beat officials to death at will, coerced chief clerk Sun Jin to death, and now again falsely charges dutiful officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mao wrote: "Xuan falsely claimed imperial clubs, beat officials to death, drove clerk Sun Jin to suicide, and now frames dutiful men.

sentences.zh: 乞治宣罪，還鑾、守約故任。」

translations.literal: I beg that Xuan be punished and Luan and Shouyue restored to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Punish Xuan and restore Luan and Shouyue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復偕諸給事言：「臣等屢建白，不擇可否，一概留中。

translations.literal: Before long he again joined the supervising secretaries in saying: "We have repeatedly submitted proposals, but without distinguishing merit they are all kept at the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined colleagues: "We memorialize repeatedly, yet all papers are kept at the palace.

sentences.zh: 萬一奸人陰結黨類，公行阻遏，朝有大事，陛下不聞，大臣不知，禍可勝言！」

translations.literal: If by chance evil men secretly form factions and openly obstruct, and the court has great affairs while Your Majesty hears nothing and ministers know nothing—disaster is beyond words!
translations.idiomatic: If villains block the court while Your Majesty hears nothing—disaster follows!

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾罷鹽法侍郎薛章，請黜太仆少卿馬陟，留御史徐文華，召還謝遷、韓文、孫交、張原、周廣、高公韶、王思等，罷遊畋射獵，復禦朝常儀，還久留邊兵，汰錦衣冗官，諸疏皆侃侃。

translations.literal: Later he also impeached and removed Salt Law Vice Minister Xue Zhang, asked that Court of Imperial Stud Vice Director Ma Zhi be dismissed, kept Censor Xu Wenhua, recalled Xie Qian, Han Wen, Sun Jiao, Zhang Yuan, Zhou Guang, Gao Gongshao, Wang Si, and others, stopped hunting and falconry, restored regular court audience, returned long-stationed frontier troops, and cut redundant Brocade Guard posts—all memorials were forthright.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Salt Law vice minister Xue Zhang, sought Ma Zhi's dismissal, kept Xu Wenhua, recalled Xie Qian, Han Wen, Sun Jiao, and others, ended hunting, restored court audience, recalled frontier troops, and cut Brocade Guard posts—all boldly argued.

sentences.zh: 江彬導帝巡幸。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin guided the Emperor on tours.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin led the Emperor on tours.

sentences.zh: 懋言：「彬梟桀憸邪，挾至尊出居庸，無大臣保護，獨處沙漠將半載。

translations.literal: Mao said: "Bin is a fierce, treacherous villain who took the Son of Heaven through Juyong without senior ministers' protection, alone in the desert for nearly half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Mao wrote: "Bin is a fierce villain who took the Emperor through Juyong without ministers, alone in the desert half a year.

sentences.zh: 兩宮違養，郊廟不親，四方災異叠見，盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: The two palaces were left unfilially, the suburban temples unattended, calamities and omens appeared in succession under heaven, and bandits rose like bees.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowagers went unfilially served, rites neglected, omens multiplied, bandits swarmed.

sentences.zh: 留彬一日，為宗社一日憂，乞立置重典。」

translations.literal: Keep Bin one day and the altars of state suffer one day's worry—I beg he be immediately punished by heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: Each day Bin remains is a day of peril—punish him at once.

sentences.zh: 時中外章奏，帝率不省視。

translations.literal: At that time memorials inside and outside the court were generally not reviewed by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from court and country went unread.

sentences.zh: 規主闕者，往往得無罪。

translations.literal: Those who admonished the ruler's faults often escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who admonished the throne often went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 一觸權幸，禍立至，人皆為懋危。

translations.literal: Touch the powerful and favorites and disaster came at once; all feared for Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Touch the powerful and disaster struck; all feared for Mao.

sentences.zh: 而彬方日侍帝娛樂，亦不之見也。

translations.literal: Yet Bin daily attended the Emperor's amusements and never saw it.
translations.idiomatic: Bin daily amused the Emperor and never saw the memorial.

sentences.zh: 請回鑾，諫南幸，懋皆與。

translations.literal: Pleading for the imperial return, remonstrating against the southern tour—Mao joined in all.
translations.idiomatic: He joined pleas for the Emperor's return and protests against the southern tour.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，帝在南都，懋從行。

translations.literal: When Prince Chen Hao rebelled the Emperor was in the southern capital and Mao followed on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chen Hao rebelled the Emperor was in Nanjing; Mao followed.

sentences.zh: 請急定平賊功賞，既又數請還京，率同官伏闕，皆不省。

translations.literal: He urgently asked that merit rewards for suppressing the rebels be settled, then repeatedly asked to return to the capital, and with fellow officials prostrated at the palace gate—all went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: He urged reward for suppressing the rebels, repeatedly begged return to the capital, and knelt at the gate with colleagues—all ignored.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東參議，遷副使。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of Guangdong and was transferred to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Posted Guangdong vice commissioner, then promoted within the province.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，有錦衣官校偵事廣東，懋與按察使張祐疑其偽，執之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing, Brocade Guard officers came to Guangdong on surveillance; Mao and Intendant Zhang You suspected they were impostors and arrested them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year four, Brocade Guard officers came to Guangdong; Mao and Intendant Zhang You suspected impostors and arrested them.

sentences.zh: 事聞，逮下詔獄，謫藤縣典史。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was arrested and sent to the imperial prison and demoted to registrar of Teng County.
translations.idiomatic: Reported, he was jailed and demoted to Teng County registrar.

sentences.zh: 屢遷至廣西布政使。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to administrative commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Guangxi administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十六年入為應天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered office as prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Year sixteen made him Yingtian prefect.

sentences.zh: 坐所進鄉試錄忤旨，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Because the provincial examination record he submitted offended the throne, he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial exam record he submitted offended the throne; he retired and died.
