sentences.zh: 王儀，字克敬，文安人。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, courtesy name Kejing, a native of Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, styled Kejing, was from Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Jiajing year two.

sentences.zh: 除靈璧知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Made magistrate of Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 以能，調嘉定。

translations.literal: For competence he was transferred to Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: For competence transferred to Jiading.

sentences.zh: 七年擢御史，巡按陜西。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to censor and toured as inspector in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven made him Shaanxi touring censor.

sentences.zh: 秦府豪占民產，儀悉奪還民。

translations.literal: The Qin princely establishment's powerful families seized people's property; Yi took it all back for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Qin princes' powerful followers seized property; Yi returned it all.

sentences.zh: 延綏大饑，朝命陜西布政使胡忠為巡撫，儀論罷之。

translations.literal: Yan-sui suffered great famine; the court ordered Shaanxi administrative commissioner Hu Zhong as grand coordinator; Yi memorialized to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-sui famine struck; the court named Hu Zhong coordinator; Yi demanded his removal.

sentences.zh: 已，巡按河南。

translations.literal: Later he toured as censor in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he toured Henan as censor.

sentences.zh: 趙府輔國將軍祐椋招亡命殺人劫奪積十余年，莫敢發。

translations.literal: Zhao princely establishment Assistant State General You Liang recruited fugitives to kill and plunder for more than ten years and no one dared expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao prince's assistant general You Liang recruited killers and plundered for ten years; none dared expose him.

sentences.zh: 儀偕巡撫吳山奏之，奪爵禁錮。

translations.literal: Yi joined Grand Coordinator Wu Shan in memorializing; his title was stripped and he was confined.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and coordinator Wu Shan memorialized; You Liang lost his title and was confined.

sentences.zh: 會儀出為蘇州知府，甫三月，祐椋潛入都，奏儀捃摭，並訐都御史毛伯溫以私憾入己罪。

translations.literal: As Yi went out as Suzhou prefect, after only three months You Liang secretly entered the capital and memorialized that Yi had fabricated charges and also falsely accused Censor-in-Chief Mao Bowen of inserting personal grudges into his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Three months into Yi's Suzhou prefecture, You Liang slipped into the capital and charged Yi with fabrication and accused Mao Bowen of bias.

sentences.zh: 且言：「臣嘗建醮祈皇嗣，為知府王天民訕笑」，請並按問。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant once held a ritual to pray for an imperial heir and was mocked by Prefect Wang Tianmin"—and asked that all be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed Yi mocked his ritual prayer for an heir and asked for a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 帝心知祐椋罪，而悅其建醮語。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew in his heart that You Liang was guilty but was pleased by his ritual-prayer words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew You Liang guilty but liked his prayer-for-heir story.

sentences.zh: 為遣使覆按，解儀、伯溫任，下天民獄。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to reinvestigate, relieved Yi and Bowen of office, and sent Tianmin to prison.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to reinvestigate, removed Yi and Bowen, and jailed Tianmin.

sentences.zh: 使者奏儀不誣，第祐椋罪在赦前，宜輕坐。

translations.literal: The envoys reported that Yi had not slandered but that You Liang's crime fell before an amnesty and should be lightly punished.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys found Yi innocent but said You Liang's crime predated an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝終憐祐椋愛己，竟復其爵，除儀名，伯溫、山、天民皆得罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately pitied You Liang's affection for himself, restored his title in the end, struck Yi's name from the rolls, and Bowen, Shan, and Tianmin all suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying You Liang's devotion, the Emperor restored his title, disgraced Yi, and punished Bowen, Shan, and Tianmin.

sentences.zh: 終嘉靖世，多以誹謗齋醮獲重禍，由祐椋訐奏始。

translations.literal: Through the whole Jiajing reign many suffered heavy punishment for slandering ritual prayer—beginning with You Liang's false memorial.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Jiajing many were ruined for mocking ritual prayer—starting with You Liang's charge.

sentences.zh: 儀去蘇州，士民走闕下乞留，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Yi left Suzhou, gentry and people went to the palace gate begging he be kept; the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi left Suzhou, people begged at the gate to keep him; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 既而薦起知撫州。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended and raised to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later recommended, he became Fuzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 蘇州士民復走闕下乞還儀，至再，不報。

translations.literal: Suzhou gentry and people again went to the palace gate begging Yi's return—a second time—and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou people again begged at the gate for Yi's return; no answer.

sentences.zh: 歸訴於巡撫侯位。

translations.literal: Returning they appealed to Grand Coordinator Hou Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They appealed to coordinator Hou Wei.

sentences.zh: 位以聞，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: Wei reported it and the Emperor then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reported it and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 至則嘆曰：「蘇賦當天下什二，而田額淆無可考，何以定賦？」

translations.literal: On arrival he sighed: "Suzhou's levy equals one-tenth of the realm, yet field quotas are confused beyond reckoning—how can levies be fixed?
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he said: "Suzhou pays a tenth of the realm's taxes, yet field rolls are chaos—how fix the levy?

sentences.zh: 乃履畝丈之，使縣各為籍。

translations.literal: He then measured fields by the mu and had each county keep its own register.
translations.idiomatic: He measured every field and had each county keep registers.

sentences.zh: 以八事定田賦，以三條核稅課，徭役、雜辦維均。

translations.literal: He fixed field levies with eight measures, verified tax items with three rules, and equalized corvée and miscellaneous charges.
translations.idiomatic: Eight rules fixed field levies, three rules verified taxes, and corvée was equalized.

sentences.zh: 治為知府第一，進浙江副使，飭蘇、松、常、鎮兵備。

translations.literal: His governance ranked first among prefects; he was promoted to vice commissioner of Zhejiang overseeing military affairs in Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Top-ranked prefect, he became Zhejiang vice commissioner over Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang defense.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫歐陽鐸均田賦，儀佐之，以治蘇者推行於旁郡。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Coordinator Ouyang Duo equalized field levies; Yi assisted him and extended Suzhou methods to neighboring prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinator Ouyang Duo equalized levies; Yi helped extend Suzhou's methods to neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 坐與操江王學夔討賊敗績，停俸戴罪。

translations.literal: Because he and River Controller Wang Xuekui failed in suppressing bandits, salary was withheld while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He and river controller Wang Xuekui failed against bandits and served with salary cut.

sentences.zh: 未幾，殪賊江中，進秩一等，遷山西右參政，分守冀、寧。

translations.literal: Before long bandits were destroyed on the river; he advanced one rank in promotion, was transferred to right vice commissioner of Shanxi, and defended Ji and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits were killed on the river; promoted one rank, he became Shanxi right vice commissioner defending Ji and Ning.

sentences.zh: 寇抵清源城，儀洞開城門，寇疑引去。

translations.literal: When raiders reached Qingyuan city Yi opened the city gate wide; the raiders suspected a trap and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders reached Qingyuan; Yi opened the gates wide and they withdrew suspecting a trap.

sentences.zh: 按行所部，築城郭，積糗糧，榆次、平定間遂皆有城。

translations.literal: Touring his jurisdiction he built walls and stockpiled grain; between Yuci and Pingding there were walls everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Touring his circuit he built walls and stored grain; Yuci and Pingding were walled.

sentences.zh: 二十一年擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-one made him Xuanfu grand coordinator, right assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 冠入龍門，總兵官郤永等敗之。

translations.literal: When raiders entered Longmen, Chief Commander Chi Yong and others defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders entered Longmen; Commander Chi Yong defeated them.

sentences.zh: 儀進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Yi advanced to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yi became vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋以築邊垣，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Soon for building the frontier wall he was granted silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received silver and silk for building the frontier wall.

sentences.zh: 寇自萬全右衛入，遊騎犯完、唐。

translations.literal: Raiders entered from Wanquan Right Guard and roaming horsemen violated Wan and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders entered from Wanquan Right Guard and harried Wan and Tang.

sentences.zh: 奪俸二級。

translations.literal: Two ranks of salary were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Two ranks of salary were cut.

sentences.zh: 考察拾遺，貶一官。

translations.literal: In the performance review for overlooked faults he was demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Performance review demoted him one rank.

sentences.zh: 已，勘上失事罪，貶秩如初。

translations.literal: Later, investigating the failure, he was demoted to his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later investigation restored the original demotion level.

sentences.zh: 久之，除肅州兵備副使，協巡撫楊博徙哈密遺種於境外。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed vice commissioner for military affairs at Suzhou and with Grand Coordinator Yang Bo moved Hami's remnant population beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Later made Suzhou military vice commissioner; with coordinator Yang Bo he moved Hami remnants beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右參政，復拜右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to right vice commissioner and again appointed right assistant censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right vice commissioner, then Gansu grand coordinator, right assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未行，俺答犯京師，詔儀馳鎮通州。

translations.literal: Before he departed Altan invaded the capital region and an edict ordered Yi to rush to secure Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Altan threatened the capital; Yi was ordered to secure Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞部卒掠民貲，捕笞之，枷市門外。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan's troops plundered people's goods; he captured and beat them and put them in the cangue at the market gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan's troops plundered civilians; Yi beat them and caged them at the market gate.

sentences.zh: 鸞訴於帝，逮訊斥為民，卒。

translations.literal: Luan complained to the Emperor; Yi was arrested, interrogated, expelled as a commoner, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Luan complained; Yi was tried, expelled, and died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，子緘訟冤，復官賜恤。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing his son Jian sued to clear the injustice; office was restored and condolence gifts granted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing son Jian cleared the injustice; office was restored and condolence granted.

sentences.zh: 緘，官按察使，分巡遼陽，以知兵名。

translations.literal: Jian served as intendant touring Liaodong and was known for military knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Liaodong intendant, was known for military skill.

sentences.zh: 王學夔，安福人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuekui was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuekui was from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 正德時，以吏部主事諫南巡，跪闕下，受杖。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel he remonstrated against the southern tour, knelt at the palace gate, and received beating.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, as a Personnel secretary he knelt at the gate protesting the southern tour and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，奏請裁戚畹，又申救言官。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing he memorialized asking to cut imperial in-laws' privileges and again interceded for censors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he sought to cut imperial in-laws' privileges and defended censors.

sentences.zh: 歷考功、文選郎中，廉謹為時所稱。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Bureaus of Evaluation and Selection and was praised by his time for integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Evaluation and Selection and was praised for integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: He once pacified Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He once pacified Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 有偽稱皇子者，諸司議用兵。

translations.literal: When someone falsely claimed to be an imperial son, various offices debated using troops.
translations.idiomatic: When a false imperial son appeared, offices debated sending troops.

sentences.zh: 學夔曰：「妄豎子耳。」

translations.literal: Xuekui said: "A deluded youth, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Xuekui said: "A deluded youth, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 密捕致之辟。

translations.literal: He secretly captured him and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京吏、禮、兵三部尚書。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to minister of personnel, rites, and war at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Nanjing minister of personnel, rites, and war.

sentences.zh: 隆慶、萬歷間，存問者再。

translations.literal: In the Longqing and Wanli reigns imperial inquiries reached him twice.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing and Wanli emperors inquired after him twice.

sentences.zh: 年九十四卒。

translations.literal: He died at age ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 曾鈞，字廷和，進賢人。

translations.literal: Zeng Jun, courtesy name Tinghe, a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jun, styled Tinghe, was from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi of Jiajing year eleven.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: Made a courier.

sentences.zh: 擢南京禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Nanjing Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Nanjing Rites supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時四方銀場得不償費，且為盜窟，鈞奏罷之。

translations.literal: At that time silver mines in all directions cost more than they yielded and also became bandit lairs; Jun memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Silver mines nationwide cost more than they yielded and bred bandits; Jun had them abolished.

sentences.zh: 鈞剛廉疾俗。

translations.literal: Jun was upright, incorrupt, and hated corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was upright, incorrupt, and hated vice.

sentences.zh: 首劾罷參贊尚書劉龍。

translations.literal: He first impeached and removed Participating Minister Liu Long.
translations.idiomatic: He first impeached and removed participating minister Liu Long.

sentences.zh: 已，劾翊國公郭勛、禮部尚書嚴嵩。

translations.literal: Later he impeached Assistant State General Guo Xun and Minister of Rites Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Then he impeached Marquis Guo Xun and Rites Minister Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 未幾劾工部侍郎蔣淦、延綏巡撫趙錦。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Vice Minister of Works Jiang Gan and Yan-sui Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Works vice minister Jiang Gan and Yan-sui coordinator Zhao Jin.

sentences.zh: 最後劾罷操江都御史柴經。

translations.literal: Finally he impeached and removed River Controller Censor-in-Chief Chai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he impeached and removed river controller Chai Jing.

sentences.zh: 直聲震一時。

translations.literal: His upright voice shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: His bold voice shook the age.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南副使。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Posted Yunnan vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 兩司詣黔國公率廷謁，鈞始正其禮，且厘還所侵麗江民地。

translations.literal: The two provincial commissions all went to the Duke of Qian State's court to pay homage; Jun first corrected the ritual and also restored Lijiang people's land that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: Both commissions bowed at the Duke of Qian's court; Jun corrected the ritual and restored seized Lijiang land.

sentences.zh: 遷四川參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Sichuan vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 黔寇亂，撫定之。

translations.literal: When Qian bandits rebelled he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian bandits rebelled he pacified them.

sentences.zh: 屢遷河南左布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left administrative commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Henan left administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十一年以右副都御史總理河道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was made right vice censor-in-chief supervising the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirty-one made him waterworks supervisor, right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 徐、邳等十七州縣連被水患，帝憂之，趣上方略。

translations.literal: Xuzhou, Pei, and seventeen other prefectures and counties suffered successive flood disasters; the Emperor was troubled and urgently asked for plans.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou, Pei, and seventeen counties suffered floods; the Emperor urgently asked for plans.

sentences.zh: 鈞請浚劉伶臺至赤晏廟八十里，築草灣老黃河口，增高家堰長堤，繕新莊等舊閘。

translations.literal: Jun asked to dredge eighty li from Liulingtai to Chiyan Temple, build the Caowan Old Yellow River mouth, raise the long dike at Gaojia Weir, and repair old sluices such as Xinzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun proposed dredging eighty li from Liulingtai to Chiyan Temple, building the Caowan Old Yellow River mouth, raising Gaojia Weir's dike, and repairing sluices including Xinzhuang.

sentences.zh: 閲數月，工成。

translations.literal: After several months the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within months the work was done.

sentences.zh: 進工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to right vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right Works vice minister.

sentences.zh: 治河四年，入為南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After four years managing the river he entered office as right vice minister of justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After four years on the river he became Nanjing Justice vice minister.

sentences.zh: 久之，乞歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he retired.

sentences.zh: 家居十余年卒。

translations.literal: Living at home more than ten years he died.
translations.idiomatic: At home ten years he died.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書，謚恭肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made minister of justice and given the posthumous name Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Justice minister, posthumous name Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鄭岳等居官，歷著風操。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zheng Yue and the others in office repeatedly displayed integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Zheng Yue and the others repeatedly showed integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 箴主闕，抑近幸，本末皆有可觀。

translations.literal: They admonished the ruler's faults and checked favorites; in root and branch all had merit worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: They admonished the throne and checked favorites—substance and detail alike commendable.

sentences.zh: 斤斤奉職，所至以治辦聞，殆列卿之良歟！

translations.literal: Conscientiously fulfilling duty, wherever they went they were known for effective governance—perhaps fine among vice ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Conscientious in duty, famed for effective rule wherever they served—perhaps among the finest vice ministers!

sentences.zh: 唐胄論安南，切於事理。

translations.literal: Tang Zhou's discussion of Annam was close to the logic of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhou on Annam was sound in logic.

sentences.zh: 歐陽鐸之均田賦，惠愛在民；

translations.literal: Ouyang Duo's equalization of field levies brought kindness and benefit to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Duo's equalization of field levies benefited the people;

sentences.zh: 令久於其任，幾與周忱比矣。

translations.literal: had he long remained in office he would nearly have compared with Zhou Chen.
translations.idiomatic: had he served longer he might have rivaled Zhou Chen.
